documentsNeeded: Approved Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
Passport valid for at least six months beyond your planned arrival date, with at least one blank page
Passport-type photo or selfie

Kenyan Government travel health insurance (mandatory from 5 October 2026; Kenya's insurance portal says non-Kenyans visiting for less than 3 months must buy it, while the UK and Canadian governments say stays under 12 months): up to USD 44 per person, one policy per traveller, bought as part of the eTA application or on the eCitizen insurance portal; your own travel insurance doesn't replace it. It covers up to 3 months, with multiple entries.
notes: Standard eTA fee is USD 30 for a single entry; the eTA itself is valid for travel within 90 days of issuance (you must enter Kenya within that window). The actual length of stay granted is set by the immigration officer at the point of entry (Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Regulations, 2012, reg. 30(3): a visitor's pass is capped at 6 months from the date of entry, at the officer's discretion) — there is no single published guaranteed number of days for eTA holders, so no day count is shown here. American nationals also have the option of a Five-Year Multi-Entry eTA (USD 185) in addition to the Standard single-entry eTA (USD 30).

documentsNeeded: Passport or other genuine travel document valid for at least 6 months
Passport-style photo (required if applying in advance via the Irembo government portal)
notes: Rwanda has granted visa-on-arrival access to citizens of all countries since 1 Jan 2018 (no prior application required — DGIE 'Visa on arrival' policy page). American nationals are not from a country that is a member of the African Union, Commonwealth, or La Francophonie, and the United States is not on Rwanda's named 90-day visa-free list, so the standard Holiday/Tourism (V1) visa applies: USD 50 for a single-entry visa valid 30 days, or USD 70 for a multiple-entry visa valid 90 days (Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration — Visitors visa, V1 Holiday visa terms). The visa can be obtained online in advance via the Irembo government portal, at a Rwandan diplomatic mission, or directly on arrival at Kigali International Airport or any land border. Ebola: Rwanda screens arrivals at Kigali airport and restricts its border with the DRC; Germany's advice says foreign travellers who were in the DRC in the 30 days before arrival, even in transit, are refused entry.

documentsNeeded: Approved Egypt e-Visa, obtained in advance online via the Egypt e-Visa Portal (visa2egypt.gov.eg) — single-entry USD 30 or multiple-entry USD 65
Passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival
Printed e-Visa to present to the immigration officer at the port of entry
Travel itinerary
Hotel booking / accommodation details for the stay
notes: American passport holders are on the Egypt e-Visa Portal's own list of nationalities eligible to apply for an e-Visa (the FAQ page says a foreign citizen "generally must first obtain an e-Visa via the Egypt e-Visa Portal" and that eligible nationals "may be issued with an e-Visa upon application on the Egypt e-Visa Portal" — this is legally a visa, issued entirely online without an embassy visit, not a lighter-weight travel authorisation, so it is shown here as a visa). The e-Visa portal does not publish a specific permitted-stay length (number of days) anywhere in its publicly reachable FAQ, About, How-to-Apply, Disclaimer or Terms pages — the commonly repeated "30 days" figure on travel-blog and visa-agency sites was not confirmed against this or any other primary Egyptian government source, so no day count is shown rather than guessed. The e-Visa is not available to holders of Diplomatic, Service, Special, Official, Temporary, Nansen, Refugee, Mission, Alien's, or July-51-Agreement passports — those travelers must apply at an Egyptian embassy or consulate instead.

Passport valid for at least 6 months
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
Online landing and departure cards, completed before entry and exit (Nigeria Immigration Service)
Online health declaration (Nigeria Health Declaration Form), completed before you travel
notes: The Nigeria Immigration Service states the Tourism Visa (F5A) is for "citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements". Israel is not an ECOWAS member, and no primary source found names it as having a visa-waiver agreement with Nigeria for ordinary passports (NIS publishes no such list). Fees were not verified — confirm on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng). Health declaration: Canada's travel advice says all travellers must complete an online health declaration form before travelling to Nigeria; the UK's says it's required for travellers coming from countries with Ebola transmission.

documentsNeeded: Approved Morocco eVisa (Autorisation Électronique de Voyage, applied for online via acces-maroc.ma) or a consular visa
Valid passport
Supporting documents for the eVisa application (confirmed travel itinerary, accommodation, proof of means)
notes: Israel does not appear on Morocco's visa-exemption list (consulat.ma) and Israeli passport holders require a visa to enter Morocco. Since 10 July 2022, Israeli nationals are one of the first two nationalities (with Thailand) named by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as eligible for the "eVisa" fast-track via acces-maroc.ma instead of an in-person consulate visit — processed within 24h (express) or 72h (standard); the eVisa is a one-time authorization valid for up to 180 days from issue, within which it allows a stay of up to 30 days. This is based on a 2022 Ministry press release; given how diplomatically sensitive Morocco–Israel entry policy can be, re-confirm immediately before travel rather than relying solely on this record. A standard consular visa application remains the fallback route if eVisa eligibility has changed.

timedSteps.line: Approved e-Tourist Visa / Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), applied for online at indianvisaonline.gov.in at least 4 days before arrival
e-Arrival Card, completed online up to 72 hours before you arrive (it isn't a visa)

notes: India's e-Tourist Visa (e-T1 V) is issued as an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA): duration "One Month (30 Days)" from the date of first arrival, multiple entries permitted within that window, non-extendable and non-convertible. Longer 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist Visa options also exist (multiple entries), but both cap total stay at 180 days per calendar year rather than granting a longer single visit — this row reflects the standard 30-day option. Applicants must hold a passport valid at least 6 months from the date of application and show a return/onward ticket and sufficient funds; apply online at least 4 days before arrival. Diplomatic/official passport holders, and applicants of Pakistani origin or holding a Pakistani passport, are not eligible for any e-Visa category.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport (minimum 6 months validity beyond stay)
Visa application lodged in person or via the Saudi Embassy/Consulate (regular visa, not eVisa)
Supporting documents as required by the embassy (proof of accommodation, sufficient funds, itinerary, passport photos)
notes: Brazil is NOT on Saudi Arabia's official eVisa-eligible country list; the official Saudi eVisa portal directs applicants from non-listed countries to the nearest Saudi Arabia Embassy/Consulate for a regular (non-electronic) visa. Per Saudi Press Agency (official state news agency) reporting on the eVisa program's scope, Brazilian nationals holding a valid, previously-used US, UK, or Schengen visa, or holding permanent residency in the EU/GCC/UK/US, may alternatively qualify for the eVisa regardless of nationality — this alternate pathway was not independently re-confirmed on the current visa.visitsaudi.com page (which returned a JS-error on the specific eligibility sub-page at time of check) and should be treated as provisional. Alternate route regardless of nationality: travelers who hold a valid US, UK, or Schengen visa that has already been used at least once to enter the issuing country/area, OR who are legal residents of the EU, UK, or US, can obtain a Saudi visa on arrival without pre-applying for the eVisa — even though this nationality is not on Saudi Arabia's standard eVisa-eligible list. This on-arrival visa is generally valid 1 year for multiple entries with stays of up to 90 days per visit. To use this route without also qualifying for the standard eVisa, travel must be on a Saudi national carrier (Saudia, flynas, or flyadeal); passport must be valid 6+ months. This is a visa-on-arrival mechanism (reopened by Saudi authorities in March 2022 and still active as of mid-2025), distinct from the pre-approved eVisa — verify current documentary requirements and any insurance/fee conditions at the airport or via visa.visitsaudi.com before travel, as the official portal could not be directly re-confirmed (blocked automated access; this note rests on convergent secondary corroboration of a named Saudi Press Agency announcement, not a directly re-read primary text).

This on-arrival visa is generally valid 1 year for multiple entries with stays of up to 90 days per visit. To use this route without also qualifying for the standard eVisa, travel must be on a Saudi national carrier (Saudia, flynas, or flyadeal); passport must be valid 6+ months. This is a visa-on-arrival mechanism (reopened by Saudi authorities in March 2022 and still active as of mid-2025), distinct from the pre-approved eVisa — verify current documentary requirements and any insurance/fee conditions at the airport or via visa.visitsaudi.com before travel, as the official portal could not be directly re-confirmed (blocked automated access; this note rests on convergent secondary corroboration of a named Saudi Press Agency announcement, not a directly re-read primary text).

documentsNeeded: Indian passport valid for at least six months
Completed online pre-arrival registration (PAR) and its notification slip, carried with the same passport used to register
Onward or return ticket
Adequate funds to cover the stay without working
notes: Indian nationals may visit or transit Hong Kong visa-free for up to 14 days per visit only after completing pre-arrival registration online. Registration is free and valid for six months, allowing multiple visits. The notification slip must be printed, signed and used together with the same Indian passport linked to the registration (a new passport means registering again). No registration is needed for holders of a valid Indian diplomatic or official passport, a valid Hong Kong entry visa, e-Channel enrolment for frequent visitors or an HKSAR Travel Pass, for operating air or sea crew, or for passengers in direct transit by air who stay in the airport transit area. If registration is unsuccessful, apply directly to the Immigration Department for an entry visa: it normally takes four weeks after all documents are received, and Chinese diplomatic and consular missions don't accept these applications, so allow enough time. Visitors may not take up employment (paid or unpaid), start or join a business, or study, and can't normally change status after arrival; to stay longer than the visa-free period you must obtain a visa or entry permit before travelling.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
Boarding card

Useful at the border if asked: travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, health/travel insurance covering your stay, accommodation details, and any invitation or letter explaining the purpose of your visit
notes: US nationals are on Ireland's non-visa-required list (official INIS table), so no visa or pre-clearance is needed to visit. Ireland has no ETA-style pre-travel authorisation. On arrival by air or sea from outside the State you must present to an Immigration Officer, who decides how long you may stay — INIS: "up to a maximum of 3 months" — and stamps your passport; the officer can still refuse entry if not satisfied by your documents or explanations. Staying beyond 90 days requires applying to Immigration Service Delivery for permission. Ireland is not in Schengen: days here do not count toward the 90/180-day Schengen limit, and a Schengen visa or stay does not entitle you to enter Ireland. If you arrive via Northern Ireland you must still report to an Immigration Officer within 30 days (7 days if for business or employment).

Valid passport
Boarding card
Supporting documents for the Immigration Officer: proof of funds, accommodation details, itinerary, insurance and the visa application papers
notes: Chinese (People's Republic of China) nationals are on Ireland's visa-required list (official INIS table). Two routes exist: (1) apply for an Irish short-stay visa (a 'C' visa is valid for up to 3 months per Citizens Information; the Immigration Officer still decides admission and length of stay, up to 90 days); or (2) if you are living in China you may use the British Irish Visa Scheme / Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme: a UK short-stay visitor visa lets you visit Ireland without a separate Irish visa, but only if you have first landed and gained lawful entry to the UK on that visa (each separate UK leave period, up to 180 days, needs a fresh UK entry before travelling to Ireland). Visas endorsed 'BIVS' must be used in the issuing country first. A visa never guarantees entry. The Hong Kong and Macau SARs are on the non-visa list; this row applies to People's Republic of China passport holders generally.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from Albania and issued within the last 10 years
Return/onward ticket (may be requested)
Confirmation of accommodation (may be requested)
International certificate of vaccination if arriving from a country affected by an epidemic disease
notes: The U.S. Embassy in Tirana states directly: "U.S. citizens do not need a visa to enter the Republic of Albania; U.S. citizens generally are allowed to stay in Albania for up to one year without a residence permit." This is a long-standing bilateral arrangement, far more generous than the 90/180-day rule most other nationalities get. To "restart the clock" on the one-year limit you must leave Albania and stay out for at least 90 days; shorter trips abroad do not reset it. Staying beyond one year, taking a job, or enrolling in school requires a residence permit. Passport validity: Albania's own visa rules for foreigners (Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, "Regjimi i vizave për të huajt", section II: https://punetejashtme.gov.al/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/II-NR.3-REGJIMI-I-VIZAVE-PER-TE-HUAJT-INFO-PER-TE-HUAJT.pdf, checked 2026-10-18) require at least 3 months after the date you leave, and issue within the last 10 years. The U.S. Embassy says "at least three months of remaining validity" and recommends six months from your planned departure.

Corrected 2026-10-05 from a flat 90 days per entry to 90 days within 180: Albania's Law No. 79/2021 "On Foreigners" (Art. 29(2), as amended 2025) gives visa-exempt foreigners 90 days within 180 days from entry, unless a bilateral agreement or Council of Ministers decision provides otherwise; after using 90 days you may re-enter once the 180-day period has passed (Art. 29(3)). notes: Code 4 in Brazil's current QGRV (26 Aug 2026): visa exemption for up to 90 days (no 90/180 marker). Counting: Brazil's Decreto 9.199/2017 (art. 20 §1, applicable to visa-exempt visitors under art. 23) counts a visitor's stay from the first entry and pauses it while you are outside Brazil, so days add up across visits within a 12-month 'migratory year' starting at your first entry; the Federal Police may extend the stay by up to 90 days, to a maximum of 180 days per migratory year (https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2017/decreto/d9199.htm). We show the stricter limit of 90 days in any 365 so a plan that fits here also fits the rule — check with the Federal Police if you need longer.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport from France (an eVisitor-eligible country)
eVisitor (subclass 651) granted before travel — apply online while outside Australia
notes: France is on Home Affairs' eVisitor (subclass 651) eligible-passport list. The eVisitor is free, multiple entry, and valid for 12 months from grant; you can stay up to 3 months after each entry. Shown as a travel authorisation for consistency with the existing Australian ETA (subclass 601) rows: both are electronic authorisations granted before travel with no embassy application, even though Australian law treats both as visas. Home Affairs states the stay as '3 months' (not a day count) — we count that as 90 days, as for ETA holders. You must be outside Australia when you apply and when it is decided.

documentsNeeded: NZeTA (New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority) approved before travel
Passport valid for at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand
Evidence of onward travel and enough funds (may be asked for on arrival)
IVL (International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy) paid as part of the NZeTA request
New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD), free: online or in the app before you travel, or on arrival
notes: France is on Immigration New Zealand's visa waiver countries and territories list with no passport conditions attached. Visa-waiver visitors get a Visa Waiver Visitor Visa on arrival for up to 3 months, but must request an NZeTA first (from NZD $17; allow 72 hours; valid 2 years). Overall cap: up to 6 months in any 12-month period. Source for stay/validity/fee: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/new-zealand-electronic-travel-authority-nzeta/. The NZeTA request also includes the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD $100, paid together (Immigration New Zealand, Visa Waiver Visitor Visa page, checked 2026-10-05).

notes: French ordinary-passport holders are on Thailand's 30-day visa-exemption list (60 countries/territories, EU listed as a bloc) that replaced the former 60-day scheme from 15 September 2026, after Ministry of Interior notifications were published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026 (Gazette site itself not reachable for automated checks). Tourism only — other purposes need a visa. An extension of up to 30 days may be requested from the Immigration Bureau (Royal Thai Embassy London). People who entered under the old 60-day scheme before 15 September 2026 keep the stay they were granted. Cross-checked: the French MFA (diplomatie.gouv.fr, updated 15 Sep 2026) confirms the 30-day limit from 15 September 2026. You may be asked to show enough money for your stay: the UK's advice says at least THB 10,000 per person (20,000 per family); Germany's says at least THB 20,000 in cash.

notes: The Egypt e-Visa Portal (Ministry of Interior, visa2egypt.gov.eg/eVisa/FAQ, checked 2026-10-02) lists France among nationalities eligible for an e-Visa (tourism: single entry US$30, multiple entries US$65; passport valid 6 months from arrival). On arrival: French travel advice says the tourist visa can be bought on arrival at every Egyptian international airport (24-hour counters, cash in USD or EUR; US$30 single / US$60 multiple) and runs for an initial one month, extendable (legal source). French nationals may also enter with a national ID card valid at least 6 months after the return date (per French travel advice). No fixed day count is published here: Egypt's own portal does not state the permitted stay, and EU governments describe it differently (30 days for NL/ES, 'one month' for FR, 28 days for IT, not stated by DE) — check the date on the visa you are given. Working, including journalism, is not allowed on a tourist visa.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for not less than 6 months from the date of arrival in Sri Lanka
Approved Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) obtained before arrival (keeping a copy of the ETA approval notice is advised)
Confirmed return ticket
Sufficient funds to meet expenses during the stay
notes: Sri Lanka requires an ETA for all foreign visitors. United States ('UNITED STATES OF AMERICA') is one of the 40 countries whose nationals, with effect from 25.05.2026, 'are eligible to obtain tourist visa (ETA) free-of-charge for a period of 30 days' (diplomatic, official, service and ordinary passports). ETA fees paid before 25.05.2026 are non-refundable. The ETA gives a 30-day tourist visa with double entry: the second entry must fall within the 30 days from first arrival, and only the balance of those 30 days is granted on the second visit. Extension: the DI&E 'How to Extend Short Visit ETA' page says a short visit visa can be extended up to a maximum of 270 days from arrival (30 days on entry, 60 days at the first extension, 90 days at the second and third), applied for at the Visa Section of the Department of Immigration & Emigration head office (Battaramulla) or via the online e-Visa Extension portal (eservices.immigration.gov.lk) 'for extension up to 6 months'; the 'How to submit an ETA application' page instead says the ETA 'can be extended for up to six months' — the two DI&E pages conflict, so the safe reading is up to 6 months unless the department confirms more. Extension fees are charged even for holders of a free ETA. Other ETA rules from DI&E: an ETA holder must enter within three months of the ETA's issue (the FAQ separately says an ETA 'is valid for six months' — a conflict on the same site); you cannot obtain a fresh ETA while inside Sri Lanka; fees are non-refundable. A visa on arrival is also listed in the fee table (US$60 tourist for non-South-Asian nationals), but DI&E states all foreign nationals 'are required to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) prior to their arrival', so apply in advance. Beware lookalike paid ETA sites — the only official portal is eta.gov.lk. Children under 12 of any nationality get a free 30-day tourist ETA. Documents and extension rules are from the same eta.gov.lk site: visainfo/apply.jsp (port-of-entry requirements), visainfo/extsheta.jsp (extensions), visainfo/center.jsp and visainfo/faq.jsp.

legal_source.name: Fees — Online Visa Application (ETA), Department of Immigration & Emigration, Sri Lanka

documentsNeeded: Ordinary passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry to Peru
Entry is recorded digitally at international airports (virtual Tarjeta Andina de Migración, TAM); if entering by land, make sure your passport is stamped
Immigration/customs may ask for a return or onward ticket, accommodation details and proof of sufficient funds
notes: United States ordinary passport holders are visa-exempt for tourism in Peru (Peru's Foreign Ministry table, PDF dated 16 Jul 2026, legal basis D.S. N° 23-95-RE). The table marks the tourist term as '90*', defined as '90 days, extendable once for an equal period, within a period of 365 days counted from the first entry into national territory'. So the automatic allowance is 90 days, and one extension of up to 90 more days (180 total) within the 365 days that start on your first entry is possible; we model the stricter 90 days per 365-day window. The extension is applied for with Migraciones while your stay is still valid; we did not find a current Migraciones page giving the fee and procedure for non-Andean tourists, so check with Migraciones. Business visits that are not visa-exempt in the table need a business visa. Passport validity: the Embassy of Peru in Singapore's visa FAQ (gob.pe, 22 Mar 2026) says the passport 'must have a minimum of 6 months validity from the date of entry to Peru'; the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice say the same. Air arrivals are not stamped; Migraciones records entry digitally (virtual TAM) and you can check your authorised stay online at Migraciones; land arrivals must get an entry stamp (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Global Affairs Canada says officials may ask for a return/onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, and that overstaying incurs a fine for each day, payable on exit. Law: Decreto Legislativo 1350 (Migraciones) as amended by D.Leg. 1582 (El Peruano) sets the tourist stay at 'up to 183 calendar days, cumulative over a 365-day period counted from the first regular entry', or the shorter term fixed in a visa-waiver agreement; where less than 183 days is granted an extension can be granted up to that limit unless the agreement sets a lower term or forbids extension. Tourist status does not allow paid work.

Proof of onward or return travel (may be requested)
notes: The Dominican Foreign Ministry (MIREX) visa-requirements tool, queried for United States / ordinary passport / tourist visa (TS), answers '¿Requiere visa? NO'. UK and Canadian government advice both say tourists can visit visa-free for up to 30 days. Stay: the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) service page 'Prórroga de estadía para turistas' (migracion.gob.do/servicio/prorroga-de-estadia/) says tourists are allowed '30 días establecidos para los turistas' and that a stay of more than 30 days can be authorised 'a través de una prórroga extensible hasta 120 días'. Extension: apply online at the DGM portal (personal.migracion.gob.do / servicios.migracion.gob.do) with a copy of the passport data page, the stamp/date of last entry, a return air ticket, proof of own funds and a medical certificate; processing three working days; the application is free but the stay fee is charged: RD$3,500 for 30–90 days and RD$5,600 for 90–120 days, payable online or at the airport. Overstay: DGM's 'Servicio de cálculo y pago de tasas de estadía' says foreigners who exceed their authorised stay regularise it on departure by paying the stay fee (table: 30–90 days RD$3,500; 3–9 months RD$5,600; 9–12 months RD$7,000; rising to RD$98,000 for 10 years plus RD$7,000 per extra year), calculated at stayfee.migracion.gob.do. DGM's FAQ adds that if the stay fee is paid in advance at DGM you then have 30 days to leave. Canada's travel advice (travel.gc.ca, updated 26 May 2026) says to request the extension before the tourist card expires and that overstayers 'could be deported or refused re-entry'. Arrival form: DGM states the electronic E-Ticket (eticket.migracion.gob.do) is mandatory for every passenger on entry and on exit (combined migration and customs declaration, laws 285-04, 115-17, 72-02 and 226-06); UK advice says it can be completed up to 7 days before arrival and gives a QR code. Tourist card: the tax authority DGII says foreigners entering without a consular visa must have a Tourist Card (US$10, or €10 at sea/land ports only), with exemptions for nationals covered by bilateral agreements ratified by Congress; for air arrivals its cost is included in the airline ticket. The MIREX tool does not say whether this nationality is card-exempt. UK and Canadian advice both say you may be asked for proof of onward/return travel; Canada adds proof of adequate funds and your address in the country. Passport: under DGM's measure announced 2 December 2025 (memorandum continuing Resolución DGM-01-2024 of 31 May 2024), citizens of Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, the USA, 'Inglaterra' and EU countries travelling exclusively for tourism need a passport valid only for the length of their stay and departure, instead of the 6-month minimum 'que usualmente se exige'. This applies from 1 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2026 — re-check for travel in 2027.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay

notes: Visa-free: 'Estados Unidos de América' is on the list in Art. 3 literal A of Resolución 5488 de 2022 (as modified by Res. 12189 de 2026), whose holders may 'ingresar, permanecer y salir de Colombia, exentos de requisito de visa' for airport transit or short-stay activities (short stay defined as under 90 days, extendable up to 180 days) that are not paid in Colombia. Colombian law: visitors from visa-exempt countries get a Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia (PIP) at the border. A Tourism Permit (PT) is 'hasta por noventa (90) días calendario' per entry (Resolución 3167 de 2019 Art. 14, Migración Colombia). Migración Colombia counts each foreigner's days so they do not exceed 180 calendar days, continuous or discontinuous, in the same calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec). Extension: the Permiso Temporal de Permanencia (PTP, 'prórroga') extends a Tourism Permit by up to 90 more calendar days, never beyond 180 days in the calendar year; apply online (Formulario Único de Trámites) at least 5 business days before the PIP expires; 2026 fee COP 150,000 (Resolución 0599 de 2026); issued by email 3 business days after payment; grant is discretionary. Modelled here as 180 days in any 365-day window, which is stricter than the legal calendar-year count (the legal rule would allow, e.g., 180 days ending 31 Dec and a new allowance from 1 Jan) — and each single entry is still capped at 90 days unless extended. Entry documents (Migración Colombia 'Requisitos de entrada y salida del país'): valid passport, plus 'tiquete de viaje de salida y demostrar solvencia económica, según corresponda'; officers may also ask for invitation letters or lodging (Res. 3167/2019 Art. 8 par. 2). Any paid activity requires a visa. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 h to 1 h before travel) is free and explicitly 'no es de carácter obligatorio' per Migración Colombia; the UK agrees, but France's and Germany's advice say it's required before entry and exit and that airlines check it. Conflict noted: gov.uk (FCDO, updated 2026-10-06) says visitors may extend 'by up to 120 days' and 'cannot remain... more than 180 days in any 12-month period'; the Colombian sources (PTP page, Res. 3167/2019) say a 90-day PTP and 180 days per calendar year — the Colombian rule controls. Travel advice (gov.uk) adds: yellow-fever vaccination certificate required if arriving from certain countries with transmission risk; Colombian dual nationals must enter and leave on their Colombian document. The Netherlands' advice also says to report your trip in advance with the online Check-MIG form.

Extension: the Permiso Temporal de Permanencia (PTP, 'prórroga') extends a Tourism Permit by up to 90 more calendar days, never beyond 180 days in the calendar year; apply online (Formulario Único de Trámites) at least 5 business days before the PIP expires; 2026 fee COP 150,000 (Resolución 0599 de 2026); issued by email 3 business days after payment; grant is discretionary. Modelled here as 180 days in any 365-day window, which is stricter than the legal calendar-year count (the legal rule would allow, e.g., 180 days ending 31 Dec and a new allowance from 1 Jan) — and each single entry is still capped at 90 days unless extended. Entry documents (Migración Colombia 'Requisitos de entrada y salida del país'): valid passport, plus 'tiquete de viaje de salida y demostrar solvencia económica, según corresponda'; officers may also ask for invitation letters or lodging (Res. 3167/2019 Art. 8 par. 2). Any paid activity requires a visa. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 h to 1 h before travel) is free and explicitly 'no es de carácter obligatorio' per Migración Colombia; the UK agrees, but France's and Germany's advice say it's required before entry and exit and that airlines check it. Conflict noted: gov.uk (FCDO, updated 2026-10-06) says visitors may extend 'by up to 120 days' and 'cannot remain... more than 180 days in any 12-month period'; the Colombian sources (PTP page, Res. 3167/2019) say a 90-day PTP and 180 days per calendar year — the Colombian rule controls. Travel advice (gov.uk) adds: yellow-fever vaccination certificate required if arriving from certain countries with transmission risk; Colombian dual nationals must enter and leave on their Colombian document. documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay
Onward or return ticket (may be requested at the border)
Proof of sufficient funds (may be requested at the border)
notes: Visa-free: 'Brasil' is on the list in Art. 3 literal A of Resolución 5488 de 2022 (as modified by Res. 12189 de 2026), whose holders may 'ingresar, permanecer y salir de Colombia, exentos de requisito de visa' for airport transit or short-stay activities (short stay defined as under 90 days, extendable up to 180 days) that are not paid in Colombia. Colombian law: visitors from visa-exempt countries get a Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia (PIP) at the border. A Tourism Permit (PT) is 'hasta por noventa (90) días calendario' per entry (Resolución 3167 de 2019 Art. 14, Migración Colombia). Migración Colombia counts each foreigner's days so they do not exceed 180 calendar days, continuous or discontinuous, in the same calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec). Extension: the Permiso Temporal de Permanencia (PTP, 'prórroga') extends a Tourism Permit by up to 90 more calendar days, never beyond 180 days in the calendar year; apply online (Formulario Único de Trámites) at least 5 business days before the PIP expires; 2026 fee COP 150,000 (Resolución 0599 de 2026); issued by email 3 business days after payment; grant is discretionary. Modelled here as 180 days in any 365-day window, which is stricter than the legal calendar-year count (the legal rule would allow, e.g., 180 days ending 31 Dec and a new allowance from 1 Jan) — and each single entry is still capped at 90 days unless extended. Entry documents (Migración Colombia 'Requisitos de entrada y salida del país'): valid passport, plus 'tiquete de viaje de salida y demostrar solvencia económica, según corresponda'; officers may also ask for invitation letters or lodging (Res. 3167/2019 Art. 8 par. 2). Any paid activity requires a visa. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 h to 1 h before travel) is free and explicitly 'no es de carácter obligatorio' per Migración Colombia; the UK agrees, but France's and Germany's advice say it's required before entry and exit and that airlines check it. Conflict noted: gov.uk (FCDO, updated 2026-10-06) says visitors may extend 'by up to 120 days' and 'cannot remain... more than 180 days in any 12-month period'; the Colombian sources (PTP page, Res. 3167/2019) say a 90-day PTP and 180 days per calendar year — the Colombian rule controls. Travel advice (gov.uk) adds: yellow-fever vaccination certificate required if arriving from certain countries with transmission risk; Colombian dual nationals must enter and leave on their Colombian document. The Netherlands' advice also says to report your trip in advance with the online Check-MIG form.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay
Onward or return ticket (may be requested at the border)
Proof of sufficient funds (may be requested at the border)
notes: Visa-free under the EU–Colombia short-stay visa waiver agreement (in force since December 2015): Art. 4(1) 'Citizens of the Union may stay in the territory of Colombia for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period'; Art. 4(3) leaves Colombia free to extend beyond 90 days under national law. 'Francia' is also on Colombia's own visa-exempt list (Res. 5488 de 2022 Art. 3 lit. A). Modelled as the agreement's 90 days in any rolling 180-day window. Under Colombian national law a Tourism Permit is up to 90 days per entry and can be extended by a PTP 'prórroga' of up to 90 days, never beyond 180 days per calendar year; per Resolución 0599 de 2026 Art. 2 and Migración Colombia's PTP page, citizens of European Union countries are exempt from the COP 150,000 PTP fee ('UNIÓN EUROPEA - PTP - Prórroga COP 0'). Apply online at least 5 business days before the permit expires; grant is discretionary. Entry documents (Migración Colombia): valid passport, plus onward ticket and proof of funds 'según corresponda'. Check-Mig online pre-registration: sources conflict. Migración Colombia and the UK's advice say it's free and not mandatory; France's and Germany's advice say it's required within 72 hours before entry and before exit, and that airlines check it. Paid activities require a visa (the agreement excludes paid activity). Yellow-fever certificate needed if arriving from certain transmission-risk countries (gov.uk). The Netherlands' advice also says to report your trip in advance with the online Check-MIG form.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport (valid for the whole stay)
notes: Argentina's immigration authority (Dirección Nacional de Migraciones, DNM) lists no visa requirement for ordinary passports of this nationality in its 'Régimen de Visas' table (read 2026-10-09). Argentina's official tourist-entry page (argentina.gob.ar/migraciones/documentacion-para-ingresar-al-pais-como-turista) says tourists may stay 'hasta TRES (3) MESES PRORROGABLE POR OTRO PERÍODO SIMILAR' (up to 3 months, extendable once for a similar period) and may not do paid work; the Cancillería tourist-visa page and consulates express the tourist stay as 90 days, so it is modelled as 90 days per entry. Extension: request it from Migraciones before your permitted stay ends; no fee was stated on the pages read. Health insurance: Decreto 366/2025 (Boletín Oficial 29/05/2025) changed art. 34 of Migration Law 25.871 so that foreigners must present a sworn declaration of the purpose of entry and that they hold health insurance, but its new art. 123 bis says that declaration 'será exigible una vez reglamentada su implementación' (only enforceable once regulated); no implementing regulation was found as of 2026-10-09, so it is not listed as a required document. Outside emergencies, national public hospitals may charge foreigners without permanent residence (new art. 8), so insurance is strongly advisable. Cross-check not possible: travel.state.gov was blocked (Cloudflare) from this environment; status rests on the DNM table.

_sources.name: Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores (Spain) — Recomendaciones de viaje, Documentación y visados

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival
Visa on arrival (JOD 40 single entry) or a Ministry of Interior e-visa obtained in advance (mandatory in advance if entering via King Hussein/Allenby Bridge)
Police registration within 14 days if staying more than 14 days (since 1 October 2025; JOD 200 fine if missed)
notes: Permitted length of stay is not stated by any Jordanian authority we could read: the Ministry of Interior's fee table lists visa VALIDITY tiers (3 months single entry JOD 40, 3 months double JOD 60, 6 months multiple JOD 120, 1 year, 5 years), not a stay length, and traveller governments disagree (Japan MOFA: 90-day stay permit; UK: visa 'valid for 3 months'; France and Spain: 1 month). We therefore show no day count — the stay is whatever your visa states; confirm at the border. Netherlands (last changed 08-09-2026): a visa is needed; buy it on arrival at the airport or a border post (card or cash) or arrange an e-visa online in advance. Passport must be valid 6 months on arrival. Stays over 14 days require police registration or a JOD 200 fine on departure; Jordan Pass tourist visa, transit and Hajj visa holders are exempt. Children also need their own passport and visa. None of this passport's country appears on Jordan's Ministry of Interior list of 'restricted' nationalities that need prior approval (the list covers 14 Asian, 37 African and 2 Latin American states — Belize and Cuba; page footer 'Last update: 09/11/2025'), so no prior approval is needed. Visa on arrival: the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities' official Jordan Pass FAQ says non-restricted nationalities get a visa on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport and Sheikh Hussein Bridge (Jordan River crossing); at Wadi Araba (Eilat–Aqaba) it says a visa on arrival is given only to Jordan Pass holders who stay at least 2 nights, and that non-restricted nationals arriving at Aqaba airport need no visa (Aqaba Special Economic Zone). Several travellers' governments (UK, Canada, Germany, Spain) say no visa is issued on arrival at King Hussein/Allenby Bridge — get the e-visa first if you enter there. Optional e-visa in advance via the Ministry of Interior portal (eservices.moi.gov.jo). Ministry of Interior e-visa fees: 3 months single entry JOD 40; 3 months double entry JOD 60; 6 months multiple JOD 120; 1 year multiple JOD 200; 5 years multiple JOD 350. Visa fee waiver: the Jordan Pass (JOD 70–80, sold only at jordanpass.jo) waives the single-entry visa fee if you buy it before arrival and stay at least 2 consecutive nights (3 days); if you leave sooner you pay the fee on departure. Stay: the Ministry of Interior lists the standard single-entry visa as '3 months' (that is the visa's validity, not a stated stay). CONFLICT: Jordan's own Jordan Pass FAQ (© 2022) and the French (updated 15 Sep 2026) and Spanish (31 Mar 2026) travel advice still describe a 1-month/30-day initial stay extendable at a police station, while UK, Canada and Japan advice describe 3 months/90 days — check the period stamped in your passport on arrival. Stays over 14 days: since 1 October 2025 visitors staying more than 14 days must register at a police station within 14 days of arrival (biometrics), or pay a JOD 200 fine on departure; exemptions differ between sources (France, Netherlands and Spain say Jordan Pass/tourist visa, transit and Hajj visa holders are exempt; the UK says tourists are exempt). Passport must be valid at least 6 months on arrival. Land-border departure tax: UK advice says JOD 10 in cash at all land crossings (France says JOD 8).

Visa on arrival (JOD 40 single entry) or a Ministry of Interior e-visa obtained in advance (mandatory in advance if entering via King Hussein/Allenby Bridge)
Police registration within 14 days if staying more than 14 days (since 1 October 2025; JOD 200 fine if missed)
notes: Permitted length of stay is not stated by any Jordanian authority we could read: the Ministry of Interior's fee table lists visa VALIDITY tiers (3 months single entry JOD 40, 3 months double JOD 60, 6 months multiple JOD 120, 1 year, 5 years), not a stay length, and traveller governments disagree (Japan MOFA: 90-day stay permit; UK: visa 'valid for 3 months'; France and Spain: 1 month). We therefore show no day count — the stay is whatever your visa states; confirm at the border. No page from this nationality's own government was read; this row rests on Jordan's own Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities sources. None of this passport's country appears on Jordan's Ministry of Interior list of 'restricted' nationalities that need prior approval (the list covers 14 Asian, 37 African and 2 Latin American states — Belize and Cuba; page footer 'Last update: 09/11/2025'), so no prior approval is needed. Visa on arrival: the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities' official Jordan Pass FAQ says non-restricted nationalities get a visa on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport and Sheikh Hussein Bridge (Jordan River crossing); at Wadi Araba (Eilat–Aqaba) it says a visa on arrival is given only to Jordan Pass holders who stay at least 2 nights, and that non-restricted nationals arriving at Aqaba airport need no visa (Aqaba Special Economic Zone). Several travellers' governments (UK, Canada, Germany, Spain) say no visa is issued on arrival at King Hussein/Allenby Bridge — get the e-visa first if you enter there. Optional e-visa in advance via the Ministry of Interior portal (eservices.moi.gov.jo). Ministry of Interior e-visa fees: 3 months single entry JOD 40; 3 months double entry JOD 60; 6 months multiple JOD 120; 1 year multiple JOD 200; 5 years multiple JOD 350. Visa fee waiver: the Jordan Pass (JOD 70–80, sold only at jordanpass.jo) waives the single-entry visa fee if you buy it before arrival and stay at least 2 consecutive nights (3 days); if you leave sooner you pay the fee on departure. Stay: the Ministry of Interior lists the standard single-entry visa as '3 months' (that is the visa's validity, not a stated stay). CONFLICT: Jordan's own Jordan Pass FAQ (© 2022) and the French (updated 15 Sep 2026) and Spanish (31 Mar 2026) travel advice still describe a 1-month/30-day initial stay extendable at a police station, while UK, Canada and Japan advice describe 3 months/90 days — check the period stamped in your passport on arrival. Stays over 14 days: since 1 October 2025 visitors staying more than 14 days must register at a police station within 14 days of arrival (biometrics), or pay a JOD 200 fine on departure; exemptions differ between sources (France, Netherlands and Spain say Jordan Pass/tourist visa, transit and Hajj visa holders are exempt; the UK says tourists are exempt). Passport must be valid at least 6 months on arrival. Land-border departure tax: UK advice says JOD 10 in cash at all land crossings (France says JOD 8).

legal_source.name: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities (Jordan) — Jordan Pass official FAQs

documentsNeeded: Valid machine-readable passport (valid at least 1 day on entry; your stay cannot exceed its expiry)
Return or onward ticket (or navigation plan naming the destination port)
Proof of funds: at least US$100 per month or part-month of stay
Customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) on arrival
notes: Costa Rica's current visa directive (AJ-484-11-2025, in force since publication 17 Nov 2025; it repealed the Oct 2023 directive DG-30-10-2023-AJ) lists the United States (and its dependencies: Guam, US Virgin Islands, American Samoa, US Minor Outlying Islands; Puerto Rico is listed separately) in the FIRST GROUP: 'INGRESO SIN VISA. PERMANENCIA MÁXIMA: HASTA 180 DÍAS NATURALES NO PRORROGABLES. (Únicamente se prorrogará a quienes se le otorguen menos de 90 días y hasta por un máximo de 90 días). VIGENCIA MÍNIMA DE PASAPORTE: HASTA UN DÍA (el plazo de permanencia otorgado por el oficial de control migratorio, no será mayor al de la vigencia del pasaporte).' So: no visa; the border officer decides the stay, up to 180 calendar days counted from entry (per entry — the directive sets no cumulative cap across trips), and never beyond the passport's expiry; your passport only needs to be valid on the day of entry, but a longer validity buys a longer stay. The stay cannot be extended unless the officer granted fewer than 90 days, in which case an extension of up to 90 days can be requested (the text does not say whether 90 is the extra time or the total). Check the stamp: the days granted are what count, not the 180-day ceiling. Entry requirements for every foreigner (Directrices, PRIMERO §4, citing art. 42 Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 and art. 30 Reglamento de Control Migratorio 36769-G): a valid, machine-readable/biometric passport in good condition; a visa where required; proof of funds of at least US$100 per month or part-month of authorised stay; a return or onward ticket (or a navigation plan naming the destination port); and no bar to entry. Tourist (No Residente, subcategoría Turismo) status allows leisure, business or professional activities only if they involve no pay or profit in Costa Rica. Also on arrival: a customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) is required of every arriving traveller (art. 368 Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto 44051-H). Per the UK FCDO page (cross-check), a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow-fever transmission risk, an air departure tax of US$29 may apply (usually included in the ticket), and overstayers can be fined US$100 per month and refused future entry; travel.gc.ca (updated 31 Aug 2026) adds that people deported for overstaying may be barred from re-entering for 5 to 10 years.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months on arrival (MOI). Note: GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France Diplomatie, Canada and NZ advise at least 6 months — carry 6 months to be safe with airlines
Confirmed return or onward ticket
Confirmed hotel reservation in Qatar for the visit, or a clear address of a friend/relative where you will stay

Health insurance from an insurance company accredited by Qatar's Ministry of Public Health (MOI lists it as a condition of the on-arrival visa; GOV.UK/Auswärtiges Amt describe it as mandatory for stays over 30 days)
notes: Qatar MOI page 'Free On-arrival Tourist Visa for 90 Days Non-extendable for (43) Countries' lists France. Conditions: '1- Passport valid for at least three months 2- Availability of confirmed return ticket 3- Hotel reservation at any hotel in Qatar during the visit period, or a clear address of a friend or relative. 4- Health insurance from an accredited insurance company.' The stay is free of charge and NOT extendable. The Auswärtiges Amt (Germany, Stand 09.10.2026) describes this same waiver as valid for 180 days from issue, multiple entry, allowing at most 90 days of stay within that validity, and Nederland Wereldwijd says 'maximaal 90 dagen binnen 180 dagen'. Modelled as a rolling 90-days-in-180 window, the stricter representation of '90 days within a 180-day validity period'. France Diplomatie (15 Sep 2026): 'Pour les courts séjours d'une durée inférieure à 90 jours, les ressortissants français sont dispensés de visa'; return/onward ticket and proof of accommodation required; insurance compulsory for stays over 30 days. Conflict noted: MOI requires passport validity of 3 months, but several travellers' governments (GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France, Canada, NZ) say 6 months; MOI is the controlling authority, documentsNeeded flags both. Health insurance: MOI lists 'Health insurance from an accredited insurance company' as a condition of every on-arrival category and its Entry Permits page says 'A valid health insurance policy from insurance companies registered with the Ministry of Public Health is required to enter Qatar', while GOV.UK and Auswärtiges Amt say it is compulsory for stays over 30 days (GOV.UK: standard premium QAR 50 per person per month). VisitQatar notes 'Visa-free entry is now the new term defining previously visa on arrival. Nothing changed except the name.' Entry is at the discretion of the border officer. France's travel advice says health insurance is compulsory for stays over 30 days.

notes: Chile's Foreign Ministry visa table (Cuadro de aranceles de visas de permanencia transitoria, PDF created 6 March 2026, linked from consulado.gob.cl and from SERMIG's tourist page) lists ESTADOS UNIDOS DE AMÉRICA as 'NO' under '¿Requiere visa de permanencia transitoria?' with a maximum stay ('plazo máximo estadía') of 90 days, fee US$0. So ordinary-passport holders visit visa-free for up to 90 days per entry. General rules (Servicio Nacional de Migraciones, 'Permanencia Transitoria', updated 14 Oct 2025): visitors enter as holders of a Permanencia Transitoria permit, which allows a stay 'por hasta 90 días' and cannot run past the validity of the travel document; the PDI (Policía de Investigaciones) records the permitted period on the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) at entry; visitors must have 'los medios económicos suficientes para sustentar su estadía' and may not do paid work. Extension (SERMIG 'Prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria', updated 30 Jun 2026): 'hasta noventa días corridos', 'por una sola vez', applied for online in SERMIG's Portal de Trámites Digitales before the period on your TUM expires; fee USD 100 (children and adolescents exempt); you must show means of support for the extension period and explain the reasons. Arrival: the joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration form states 'ESTA DECLARACIÓN DEBE SER LLENADA POR TODA PERSONA QUE INGRESE AL PAÍS' (adults 18+ sign and include minors' baggage); see the customs rows. The table's 'plazo máximo estadía' is the stay allowed on the permit; the 30/60/90-day figures are stated as days, not months.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole intended stay (the permit cannot run past the travel document's expiry)
Proof of sufficient means of support for the stay, if asked

Joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration (Declaración Jurada) on arrival — the form says it must be filled out by every person entering Chile; adults (18+) include accompanying minors' baggage; digital version available for Santiago airport and land border crossings, or on paper
notes: Chile's Foreign Ministry visa table (Cuadro de aranceles de visas de permanencia transitoria, PDF created 6 March 2026, linked from consulado.gob.cl and from SERMIG's tourist page) lists FRANCIA as 'NO' under '¿Requiere visa de permanencia transitoria?' with a maximum stay ('plazo máximo estadía') of 90 days, fee US$0. So ordinary-passport holders visit visa-free for up to 90 days per entry. General rules (Servicio Nacional de Migraciones, 'Permanencia Transitoria', updated 14 Oct 2025): visitors enter as holders of a Permanencia Transitoria permit, which allows a stay 'por hasta 90 días' and cannot run past the validity of the travel document; the PDI (Policía de Investigaciones) records the permitted period on the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) at entry; visitors must have 'los medios económicos suficientes para sustentar su estadía' and may not do paid work. Extension (SERMIG 'Prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria', updated 30 Jun 2026): 'hasta noventa días corridos', 'por una sola vez', applied for online in SERMIG's Portal de Trámites Digitales before the period on your TUM expires; fee USD 100 (children and adolescents exempt); you must show means of support for the extension period and explain the reasons. Arrival: the joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration form states 'ESTA DECLARACIÓN DEBE SER LLENADA POR TODA PERSONA QUE INGRESE AL PAÍS' (adults 18+ sign and include minors' baggage); see the customs rows. The table's 'plazo máximo estadía' is the stay allowed on the permit; the 30/60/90-day figures are stated as days, not months. France's travel advice says stays on Easter Island are limited to 30 days, and the Tarjeta Única Migratoria must be kept and shown on exit.

documentsNeeded: Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from Montenegro
Proof of the purpose of your stay and sufficient funds for the stay and your return or onward journey (may be requested at the border)
Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)

timedSteps.line: Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)

notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for United States of America states that nationals of the United States of America 'may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

Proof of the purpose of your stay and sufficient funds for the stay and your return or onward journey (may be requested at the border)
Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)

timedSteps.line: Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)

notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for Brazil states that nationals of Brazil 'may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport — the Embassy of Jamaica in Washington says it should have at least six months' validity (UK, Canadian, French and Spanish government advice say valid for the duration of the stay; the six-month figure is the stricter one)
Return or round-trip ticket to a country you are admissible to
Evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself during the stay
Completed Immigration/Customs C5 form (online at enterjamaica.gov.jm, run by PICA and Jamaica Customs, or on paper on arrival)
notes: Visa-free. The PICA Visa Unit country listing (13 March 2025) shows UNITED STATES OF AMERICA: 'NONE – 6 months'; PICA's web table: 'NO visa required for 6 months'. The source states 6 months, not a day count; 180 days is used here as a conservative stand-in (6 months is always at least 181 days), and the immigration officer may grant less — the date stamped in your passport governs. 6 months is also PICA's stated maximum visitor stay for non-Commonwealth citizens, so no further extension as a visitor should be expected. travel.state.gov could not be read (HTTP 403) for a US-government cross-check. Common to all visitors (Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, 'Requirements for entry into Jamaica', embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/visitor_to_jamaica): national passport with 'at least six months' validity', a return or round-trip ticket, and 'evidence of sufficient funds'; 'the decision in respect of admission and length of stay in the country rests with the Immigration Officer' at the port of entry, so the date stamped in your passport is what counts. Every passenger completes the Immigration/Customs C5 card (PICA, 'Travel Documents Required': complete and sign the C5 online or on paper; the official online form is enterjamaica.gov.jm). Extension (PICA, 'Extension of Stay', pica.gov.jm/immigration/extension-of-stays): apply to PICA before your landing time expires; 'Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island' and 'Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor'; processed within three working days. PICA fee schedule (pica.gov.jm/immigration/fees, no effective date shown): extension of stay processing fee JM$10,000, and JM$50,000 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa-exemption period. Source dates: the March 2025 PICA PDF is the newest official country list found; PICA's own web table (pica.gov.jm/immigration/entry-visa-requirements) still says 'Last updated July 19, 2023'.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months (Bahamas Immigration: 'present a passport that is valid for at least six months'; passport cards are not accepted)
Return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas
Proof of sufficient funds for the stay (or a local sponsor who will receive you)
Completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
Yellow fever vaccination certificate only if arriving from (or transiting >12 hours through) a country with yellow fever risk
notes: Visa-free for up to 8 months. Bahamas Immigration's 'Before Your Arrival' page (updated 4 Nov 2026) lists 'United States of America' among countries whose diplomatic, official and ordinary passport holders 'do not need a visa to enter The Bahamas for a stay up to eight (8) months.' The source states 8 months, not days; we model 240 days, which is never longer than any 8-month span. The officer records the period granted in your passport, and it may be shorter. US citizens are not exempt from the passport requirement: 'All persons entering The Bahamas must present a valid passport' (Immigration 'Entry Requirements', updated 5 Nov 2026). Entry criteria (Bahamas Immigration 'Before Your Arrival', updated 4 Nov 2026, under the Immigration Act, Chapter 191, Section 22): a valid return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas, no gainful employment, financial means for the stay (or a local sponsor), a passport valid for at least six months (passport cards not accepted) and a completed Disembarkation/Embarkation Card; 'admittance is not automatic', and leave to land may be refused even when these are met. How long you may stay is decided at the border: the period granted 'is recorded in your passport and is at the discretion of the Immigration Officer at the port of entry', up to 'a maximum of eight (8) months, depending on nationality' (Immigration 'Entry Requirements', updated 5 Nov 2026). Extensions: apply to the Department of Immigration before the period granted expires; in-person interview with an extension officer; non-refundable processing fee of $200.00; bring your passport, return ticket, the Immigration Landing Card, the reason for the extension, a local address, an email address and mobile number, and your sponsor's passport and address if applicable (Immigration 'Extension of Stay', updated 5 Nov 2026). Overstaying is a punishable offence. Yellow fever certificate required from travellers over 1 year arriving from (or transiting more than 12 hours through) a listed risk country (including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Kenya and others), vaccinated at least 10 days before entry.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months (UK FCDO: from arrival; Canada: beyond your planned departure)
Entry stamp / authorised-stay record from migration control on arrival (keep it — needed when leaving)
notes: Visa-free: United States is not on Ecuador's official list of nationalities that must have a visa to enter (MREMH 'Países de Régimen Especial' list on gob.ec and Cancillería 'Lista de países que deben presentar visa al ingresar al Ecuador'). Under LOMH Art. 66(6), tourists who do not need a visa receive an 'autorización de permanencia' at the official migration control point. LOMH Art. 56 (as reformed 24-X-2025): 'El plazo de permanencia autorizado como turista será de hasta 90 días en el período de un año contado a partir del primer ingreso que marca el inicio de su año cronológico, prorrogable en territorio ecuatoriano, por una sola vez hasta por 90 dias continuos adicionales, previa solicitud y pago de la tarifa respectiva'. Counting: the year starts on your first entry (not 1 January); the 90 days are a total for that year, not per entry. We model it as 90 days in any 365-day window (stricter than the law, and without the optional extension). Extension (Ministerio del Interior, gob.ec 'Emisión de prórroga de autorización de permanencia en territorio para extranjeros', updated 2025-10-31): up to 90 extra days, apply online or at a Servicio de Apoyo Migratorio with a valid passport and the extension form; cost 'el equivalente a una tercera parte del Salario Básico Unificado en el Ecuador'. With the extension the yearly maximum is 180 days. Overstay (LOMH Art. 169, falta migratoria leve 2.b): a tourist who stays past the authorised 90 days without an extension, past 180 days with one, or past 180 days when admitted for 180, is fined one 'remuneración básica unificada' (one Ecuadorian basic monthly wage). Health insurance: since the 2021 reform the LOMH (Art. 52) only says residents must hold public or private health insurance; no general insurance requirement for mainland tourists appears in the consolidated law. Galápagos (per UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice, not an Ecuadorian page we could load): tourists may stay up to 60 days (Canada: '60 days in a 1-year period'); you need a Transit Control Card bought at Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in, a return ticket to the mainland, proof of a hotel booking or host invitation, and (UK) travel health insurance. The Galápagos national-park entry fee is not stated here because no official Ecuadorian source for it could be loaded. Land arrivals: Global Affairs Canada (updated 2026-10-09) says travellers entering by land or river must present an apostilled criminal-record check covering the past five years (with a Spanish translation); minors travelling with family are generally exempt. Customs: you must file the online Formulario de Registro Aduanero (FRA) only if you bring taxable goods or USD 10,000+ in cash/bearer instruments (SENAE).

China was added when Ecuador temporarily suspended the Ecuador–China visa-exemption agreement from 1 July 2024 (announced by Cancillería, 18 June 2024; the current lists include China). Apply online only, via e-VISAS (serviciosdigitales.cancilleria.gob.ec): fees USD 50 application + USD 30 issuance, no VAT. The visa gives 'un periodo de noventa (90) días contados a partir del ingreso'. Requirements per the gob.ec page: passport valid at least six months; criminal-record certificate (over-18s) from country of origin or countries of residence in the last five years, translated and apostilled/legalised, issued no more than 180 days before the last entry; proof of lawful means of subsistence (Acuerdo Ministerial 70/2024); travel itinerary with outbound and return tickets; photo. LOMH Art. 56 (as reformed 24-X-2025) also lets Ecuador accept a tourist or residence visa from designated third countries for entry, but only as set by secondary rules — no such rule covering this nationality was found, so do not rely on a third-country visa. Entry stamp / authorised-stay record from migration control on arrival (keep it — needed when leaving)
notes: Visa-free: Netherlands is not on Ecuador's official list of nationalities that must have a visa to enter (MREMH 'Países de Régimen Especial' list on gob.ec and Cancillería 'Lista de países que deben presentar visa al ingresar al Ecuador'). Under LOMH Art. 66(6), tourists who do not need a visa receive an 'autorización de permanencia' at the official migration control point. LOMH Art. 56 (as reformed 24-X-2025): 'El plazo de permanencia autorizado como turista será de hasta 90 días en el período de un año contado a partir del primer ingreso que marca el inicio de su año cronológico, prorrogable en territorio ecuatoriano, por una sola vez hasta por 90 dias continuos adicionales, previa solicitud y pago de la tarifa respectiva'. Counting: the year starts on your first entry (not 1 January); the 90 days are a total for that year, not per entry. We model it as 90 days in any 365-day window (stricter than the law, and without the optional extension). Extension (Ministerio del Interior, gob.ec 'Emisión de prórroga de autorización de permanencia en territorio para extranjeros', updated 2025-10-31): up to 90 extra days, apply online or at a Servicio de Apoyo Migratorio with a valid passport and the extension form; cost 'el equivalente a una tercera parte del Salario Básico Unificado en el Ecuador'. With the extension the yearly maximum is 180 days. Overstay (LOMH Art. 169, falta migratoria leve 2.b): a tourist who stays past the authorised 90 days without an extension, past 180 days with one, or past 180 days when admitted for 180, is fined one 'remuneración básica unificada' (one Ecuadorian basic monthly wage). Health insurance: since the 2021 reform the LOMH (Art. 52) only says residents must hold public or private health insurance; no general insurance requirement for mainland tourists appears in the consolidated law. Galápagos (per UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice, not an Ecuadorian page we could load): tourists may stay up to 60 days (Canada: '60 days in a 1-year period'); you need a Transit Control Card bought at Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in, a return ticket to the mainland, proof of a hotel booking or host invitation, and (UK) travel health insurance. The Galápagos national-park entry fee is not stated here because no official Ecuadorian source for it could be loaded. Land arrivals: Global Affairs Canada (updated 2026-10-09) says travellers entering by land or river must present an apostilled criminal-record check covering the past five years (with a Spanish translation); minors travelling with family are generally exempt. Customs: you must file the online Formulario de Registro Aduanero (FRA) only if you bring taxable goods or USD 10,000+ in cash/bearer instruments (SENAE). The Netherlands' advice for Dutch passports says at least 6 months' validity on arrival; this row keeps the rule from its own source.

documentsNeeded: Ordinary (single-entry) visa — USD 50, online e-visa (recommended) or on arrival
Passport valid at least 6 months, with at least one unused visa page
Return ticket (must be shown at the point of entry)
Mandatory Tanzanian inbound travel insurance (NIC for mainland entry, ZIC for entry via Zanzibar)
Yellow fever vaccination certificate if arriving from or transiting a yellow-fever country
notes: United Kingdom is a Commonwealth country but is expressly excluded from the Commonwealth visa exemption ("Commonwealth countries except the United Kingdom, Canada, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand"). UK FCDO advice adds that a multiple-entry visa cannot be obtained on arrival and visas are no longer issued by the Tanzanian High Commission in London. United Kingdom appears on Tanzania Immigration's list of "Countries whose nationals can obtain a visa upon arrival" — eligible for "both the online and the on arrival Visa facility"; Immigration recommends applying online at visa.immigration.go.tz (processed within ten days). Tourists need an Ordinary (single-entry) Visa, USD 50, non-refundable. Stay: the guidelines give the Ordinary Visa "a validity of up to 90 days" (a validity figure); Canada's official travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) describes it as a "3-month tourist... single entry visa on arrival" and says stays over 90 days require applying for an eVisa in advance — so 90 days is used here. Holders who visit other East African countries may re-enter on the same visa while it is still valid. No work or business allowed. A visa grant is not a final authority to enter; the officer at the border may refuse entry. One visa covers both Mainland and Zanzibar. Mandatory inbound travel insurance: NIC's official FAQ states the cover "is mandatory to all foreigners traveling in Tanzania Mainland", entering by land, sea or air, premium the TZS equivalent of USD 44 per person, valid 92 days with multiple entries, buy online at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz or at the entry point; residents of EAC/SADC partner states are excluded (https://inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz/faqs). Canada's travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) confirms the insurer is NIC for mainland entry and the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) for entry via Zanzibar. Yellow fever: Immigration's tourist-info page says visitors must follow the Ministry of Health's yellow fever requirements; Canada's advice says proof of vaccination is required if arriving from, or transiting an airport in, a yellow-fever country. Guidelines PDF dated September 2026 (immigration.go.tz upload of 2026-09-10). Ebola: since 17 October 2026 Tanzania applies heightened health screening at all points of entry for travellers from high-risk regions; the Netherlands' advice says all travellers must fill in a health form within 24 hours before arrival or on arrival.

notes: Israel's Population and Immigration Authority (PIBA) lists United States of America as visa-exempt: the official ETA-IL eligibility checker, run on 2026-10-10 for a United States of America regular (national) passport with purpose 'Visit (Tourism)', returned 'Eligible — Based on your answers, you can apply for an ETA-IL' (the checker's country data also flags this nationality NEED_PERMIT=0). PIBA: 'As of January 1st, 2025, travelers to Israel must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey.' An approved ETA-IL lets you travel to Israel and 'stay for up to 90 days per visit'; it is valid for up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first, and a new one (another 25 NIS) is needed with a new passport or a change of name, gender or citizenship. Every traveller including minors needs their own ETA-IL (an adult applies for a minor). Replies usually come within 24–72 hours; PIBA recommends applying at least 72 hours before booking flights or hotels. Apply only on the official site israel-entry.piba.gov.il. An ETA-IL 'does not constitute a guarantee of entry' — a border control officer decides at arrival, and it can be revoked for immigration or security reasons. Not exempt: people with Israeli citizenship (including dual nationals travelling on a foreign passport — they must show proof of Israeli citizenship to the airline) or holders of a valid Israeli visa. Stays beyond 90 days need an extension request under PIBA procedures (no fee or maximum stated on the pages read). Work is not allowed on an ETA-IL.

documentsNeeded: Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from North Macedonia
Proof of the purpose and conditions of your stay, and enough money for the stay and your return or onward journey (may be requested at the border)

Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

timedSteps.line: Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs page for USA states: 'Visa for foreign citizens: Not needed'. Law on Foreigners: a short stay, with or without a visa, is 'не подолго од 90 дена во кој било период од 180 дена' (no longer than 90 days in any 180-day period preceding each day of the stay; Art. 2(9), Art. 11(1)), and a visa-free foreigner must leave 'најдоцна до истекот на рокот од 90 дена во текот на 180 дена' (Art. 21). Art. 11(1)(a): the passport must be valid at least three months after the planned departure and issued in the previous 10 years. Art. 190: paid accommodation registers a foreigner's stay within 12 hours, other hosts within 48 hours, and otherwise the foreigner registers within 48 hours of crossing the border.

notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs page for Malaysia states: 'Visa for foreign citizens: Not needed'. Law on Foreigners: a short stay, with or without a visa, is 'не подолго од 90 дена во кој било период од 180 дена' (no longer than 90 days in any 180-day period preceding each day of the stay; Art. 2(9), Art. 11(1)), and a visa-free foreigner must leave 'најдоцна до истекот на рокот од 90 дена во текот на 180 дена' (Art. 21). Art. 11(1)(a): the passport must be valid at least three months after the planned departure and issued in the previous 10 years. Art. 190: paid accommodation registers a foreigner's stay within 12 hours, other hosts within 48 hours, and otherwise the foreigner registers within 48 hours of crossing the border.
