notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for Austria states: 'Nationals of Austria may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' The same page adds: 'Nationals of Austria may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 30 days, without a visa, with a valid identity card issued by the competent authority of Austria.' Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

_sources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade of North Macedonia — Do you need a visa? (per-country visa regime for foreign citizens)

_sources.claim: 90 days in any 180 (Arts 2, 11, 21); passport 3 months after departure, issued within 10 years (Art. 11); registration 12/48 hours (Art. 190)
_sources.name: Law on Foreigners (Закон за странци), consolidated text, Ministry of Internal Affairs of North Macedonia

documentsNeeded: Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from North Macedonia
Proof of the purpose and conditions of your stay, and enough money for the stay and your return or onward journey (may be requested at the border)

Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

timedSteps.line: Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs page for Sweden states: 'Visa for foreign citizens: Not needed'. Law on Foreigners: a short stay, with or without a visa, is 'не подолго од 90 дена во кој било период од 180 дена' (no longer than 90 days in any 180-day period preceding each day of the stay; Art. 2(9), Art. 11(1)), and a visa-free foreigner must leave 'најдоцна до истекот на рокот од 90 дена во текот на 180 дена' (Art. 21). Art. 11(1)(a): the passport must be valid at least three months after the planned departure and issued in the previous 10 years. Art. 190: paid accommodation registers a foreigner's stay within 12 hours, other hosts within 48 hours, and otherwise the foreigner registers within 48 hours of crossing the border.

_sources.name: Law on Foreigners (Закон за странци), consolidated text, Ministry of Internal Affairs of North Macedonia

documentsNeeded: North Macedonian short-stay (C) visa issued before travel
Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from North Macedonia
Travel health insurance (a C visa can be refused without it)

Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

timedSteps.line: Registration of your address with the police within 48 hours of arrival if you're not in paid accommodation or staying with a host (paid accommodation registers you within 12 hours, a private host within 48 hours)

notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs page for Belarus states: 'Visa for foreign citizens: Needed'. Stays on a C visa may not exceed 90 days in any 180 (Law on Foreigners, Art. 26(2)); a visa application is refused if the applicant has no health or travel insurance (Art. 37). The pages read don't mention any exemption for holders of other countries' visas or residence permits. Law on Foreigners: a short stay, with or without a visa, is 'не подолго од 90 дена во кој било период од 180 дена' (no longer than 90 days in any 180-day period preceding each day of the stay; Art. 2(9), Art. 11(1)), and a visa-free foreigner must leave 'најдоцна до истекот на рокот од 90 дена во текот на 180 дена' (Art. 21). Art. 11(1)(a): the passport must be valid at least three months after the planned departure and issued in the previous 10 years. Art. 190: paid accommodation registers a foreigner's stay within 12 hours, other hosts within 48 hours, and otherwise the foreigner registers within 48 hours of crossing the border.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from Albania and issued within the last 10 years
notes: Albania's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs lists foreign nationals who enter and stay in the Schengen Area without a visa among those who enter Albania without a visa; Austrian citizens enter and stay in the Schengen Area without a visa as EU citizens (EU free movement). Albania's Law No. 79/2021 "On Foreigners" (Art. 29(2), as amended 2025) gives visa-exempt foreigners 90 days within 180 days from entry, unless a bilateral agreement or Council of Ministers decision provides otherwise; after using 90 days you may re-enter once the 180-day period has passed (Art. 29(3)). Register with the local border and migration authority within 10 days of entry as a rule (Art. 29(5)). Passport rule from the same MFA sheet. Albania's per-country visa table (MFA PDF) could not be retrieved; a bilateral agreement could grant a longer stay than shown here, never a shorter one.

notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for Iceland states: 'Nationals of Iceland may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' The same page adds: 'Nationals of Iceland may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 30 days, without a visa, with a valid identity card issued by the competent authority of Iceland.' Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

timedSteps.line: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival — required for every entry

notes: Icelandic ordinary-passport holders are on Thailand's 30-day visa-exemption list (60 countries/territories) that replaced the former 60-day scheme from 15 September 2026, after Ministry of Interior notifications were published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026 (Gazette site itself not reachable for automated checks). Tourism only — other purposes need a visa. An extension of up to 30 days may be requested from the Immigration Bureau (Royal Thai Embassy London). Entries under the exemption are limited to twice per calendar year: the Royal Thai Embassy London states this generally, while TAT describes the limit as applying to land-border entries — check before planning repeat visits. People who entered under the old 60-day scheme before 15 September 2026 keep the stay they were granted. You may be asked to show enough money for your stay: the UK's advice says at least THB 10,000 per person (20,000 per family); Germany's says at least THB 20,000 in cash.

timedSteps.line: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival — required for every entry

notes: Swiss ordinary-passport holders are on Thailand's 30-day visa-exemption list (60 countries/territories) that replaced the former 60-day scheme from 15 September 2026, after Ministry of Interior notifications were published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026 (Gazette site itself not reachable for automated checks). Tourism only — other purposes need a visa. An extension of up to 30 days may be requested from the Immigration Bureau (Royal Thai Embassy London). Entries under the exemption are limited to twice per calendar year: the Royal Thai Embassy London states this generally, while TAT describes the limit as applying to land-border entries — check before planning repeat visits. People who entered under the old 60-day scheme before 15 September 2026 keep the stay they were granted. You may be asked to show enough money for your stay: the UK's advice says at least THB 10,000 per person (20,000 per family); Germany's says at least THB 20,000 in cash.

documentsNeeded: NZeTA (New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority) approved before travel
Passport valid for at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand
Evidence of onward travel and enough funds (may be asked for on arrival)
IVL (International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy) paid as part of the NZeTA request
New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD), free: online or in the app before you travel, or on arrival
notes: Austria is on Immigration New Zealand's visa waiver countries and territories list with no passport conditions attached. Visa-waiver visitors get a Visa Waiver Visitor Visa on arrival for up to 3 months, but must request an NZeTA first (from NZD $17; allow 72 hours; valid 2 years). Overall cap: up to 6 months in any 12-month period. Source for stay/validity/fee: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/new-zealand-electronic-travel-authority-nzeta/. The NZeTA request also includes the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD $100, paid together (Immigration New Zealand, Visa Waiver Visitor Visa page, checked 2026-10-05).

documentsNeeded: NZeTA (New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority) approved before travel
Passport valid for at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand
Evidence of onward travel and enough funds (may be asked for on arrival)
IVL (International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy) paid as part of the NZeTA request
New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD), free: online or in the app before you travel, or on arrival
notes: San Marino is on Immigration New Zealand's visa waiver countries and territories list with no passport conditions attached. Visa-waiver visitors get a Visa Waiver Visitor Visa on arrival for up to 3 months, but must request an NZeTA first (from NZD $17; allow 72 hours; valid 2 years). Overall cap: up to 6 months in any 12-month period. Source for stay/validity/fee: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/new-zealand-electronic-travel-authority-nzeta/. The NZeTA request also includes the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD $100, paid together (Immigration New Zealand, Visa Waiver Visitor Visa page, checked 2026-10-05).

documentsNeeded: Seychelles Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before you leave home, through the Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com
Passport valid for your whole stay, until you arrive back in your home country or country of residence
A return or onward ticket for the duration of the visit
Confirmed accommodation
Enough money for your stay (at least US$150 or equivalent per day)
notes: Seychelles needs no visa. A Visitor's Permit is issued free on arrival for holidays, business or visiting friends and family, for up to three months (we count that as 90 days). It can be extended in three-month steps to a maximum of twelve months, for SCR 5,000 per extension, at permits.ics.gov.sc or the Immigration office in Victoria.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay
Return or onward ticket to next destination

Further extensions are available in increments up to a cumulative limit set by BI regulations.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport — the Embassy of Jamaica in Washington says it should have at least six months' validity (UK, Canadian, French and Spanish government advice say valid for the duration of the stay; the six-month figure is the stricter one)
Return or round-trip ticket to a country you are admissible to
Evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself during the stay
Completed Immigration/Customs C5 form (online at enterjamaica.gov.jm, run by PICA and Jamaica Customs, or on paper on arrival)
notes: Visa-free. The PICA Visa Unit country listing (13 March 2025) shows 'AUSTRIA (pta)': 'NONE – 30 days' under 'Entry visa — foreigners arriving in Jamaica', with the footnote '*** Nationals of these countries are allowed to enter Jamaica without meeting a visa requirement for the purpose of tourism or to conduct short term business for the periods indicated.' Max visitor stay with extensions for non-Commonwealth citizens: 6 months (PICA). Common to all visitors (Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, 'Requirements for entry into Jamaica', embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/visitor_to_jamaica): national passport with 'at least six months' validity', a return or round-trip ticket, and 'evidence of sufficient funds'; 'the decision in respect of admission and length of stay in the country rests with the Immigration Officer' at the port of entry, so the date stamped in your passport is what counts. Every passenger completes the Immigration/Customs C5 card (PICA, 'Travel Documents Required': complete and sign the C5 online or on paper; the official online form is enterjamaica.gov.jm). Extension (PICA, 'Extension of Stay', pica.gov.jm/immigration/extension-of-stays): apply to PICA before your landing time expires; 'Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island' and 'Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor'; processed within three working days. PICA fee schedule (pica.gov.jm/immigration/fees, no effective date shown): extension of stay processing fee JM$10,000, and JM$50,000 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa-exemption period. Source dates: the March 2025 PICA PDF is the newest official country list found; PICA's own web table (pica.gov.jm/immigration/entry-visa-requirements) still says 'Last updated July 19, 2023'.

documentsNeeded: Ordinary (single-entry) visa — USD 50, online e-visa (recommended) or on arrival
Passport valid at least 6 months, with at least one unused visa page
Return ticket (must be shown at the point of entry)
Mandatory Tanzanian inbound travel insurance (NIC for mainland entry, ZIC for entry via Zanzibar)
Yellow fever vaccination certificate if arriving from or transiting a yellow-fever country
notes: Albania appears on Tanzania Immigration's list of "Countries whose nationals can obtain a visa upon arrival" — eligible for "both the online and the on arrival Visa facility"; Immigration recommends applying online at visa.immigration.go.tz (processed within ten days). Tourists need an Ordinary (single-entry) Visa, USD 50, non-refundable. Stay: the guidelines give the Ordinary Visa "a validity of up to 90 days" (a validity figure); Canada's official travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) describes it as a "3-month tourist... single entry visa on arrival" and says stays over 90 days require applying for an eVisa in advance — so 90 days is used here. Holders who visit other East African countries may re-enter on the same visa while it is still valid. No work or business allowed. A visa grant is not a final authority to enter; the officer at the border may refuse entry. One visa covers both Mainland and Zanzibar. Mandatory inbound travel insurance: NIC's official FAQ states the cover "is mandatory to all foreigners traveling in Tanzania Mainland", entering by land, sea or air, premium the TZS equivalent of USD 44 per person, valid 92 days with multiple entries, buy online at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz or at the entry point; residents of EAC/SADC partner states are excluded (https://inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz/faqs). Canada's travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) confirms the insurer is NIC for mainland entry and the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) for entry via Zanzibar. Yellow fever: Immigration's tourist-info page says visitors must follow the Ministry of Health's yellow fever requirements; Canada's advice says proof of vaccination is required if arriving from, or transiting an airport in, a yellow-fever country. Guidelines PDF dated September 2026 (immigration.go.tz upload of 2026-09-10). Ebola: since 17 October 2026 Tanzania applies heightened health screening at all points of entry for travellers from high-risk regions; the Netherlands' advice says all travellers must fill in a health form within 24 hours before arrival or on arrival.

Passport valid at least 6 months, with at least one unused visa page
Return ticket (must be shown at the point of entry)
Mandatory Tanzanian inbound travel insurance (NIC for mainland entry, ZIC for entry via Zanzibar)
Yellow fever vaccination certificate if arriving from or transiting a yellow-fever country
notes: Iceland appears on Tanzania Immigration's list of "Countries whose nationals can obtain a visa upon arrival" — eligible for "both the online and the on arrival Visa facility"; Immigration recommends applying online at visa.immigration.go.tz (processed within ten days). Tourists need an Ordinary (single-entry) Visa, USD 50, non-refundable. Stay: the guidelines give the Ordinary Visa "a validity of up to 90 days" (a validity figure); Canada's official travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) describes it as a "3-month tourist... single entry visa on arrival" and says stays over 90 days require applying for an eVisa in advance — so 90 days is used here. Holders who visit other East African countries may re-enter on the same visa while it is still valid. No work or business allowed. A visa grant is not a final authority to enter; the officer at the border may refuse entry. One visa covers both Mainland and Zanzibar. Mandatory inbound travel insurance: NIC's official FAQ states the cover "is mandatory to all foreigners traveling in Tanzania Mainland", entering by land, sea or air, premium the TZS equivalent of USD 44 per person, valid 92 days with multiple entries, buy online at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz or at the entry point; residents of EAC/SADC partner states are excluded (https://inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz/faqs). Canada's travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) confirms the insurer is NIC for mainland entry and the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) for entry via Zanzibar. Yellow fever: Immigration's tourist-info page says visitors must follow the Ministry of Health's yellow fever requirements; Canada's advice says proof of vaccination is required if arriving from, or transiting an airport in, a yellow-fever country. Guidelines PDF dated September 2026 (immigration.go.tz upload of 2026-09-10). Ebola: since 17 October 2026 Tanzania applies heightened health screening at all points of entry for travellers from high-risk regions; the Netherlands' advice says all travellers must fill in a health form within 24 hours before arrival or on arrival.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for not less than 6 months from the date of arrival in Sri Lanka
Approved Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) obtained before arrival (keeping a copy of the ETA approval notice is advised)
Confirmed return ticket
Sufficient funds to meet expenses during the stay
notes: Sri Lanka requires an ETA for all foreign visitors. Austria ('AUSTRIA') is one of the 40 countries whose nationals, with effect from 25.05.2026, 'are eligible to obtain tourist visa (ETA) free-of-charge for a period of 30 days' (diplomatic, official, service and ordinary passports). ETA fees paid before 25.05.2026 are non-refundable. The ETA gives a 30-day tourist visa with double entry: the second entry must fall within the 30 days from first arrival, and only the balance of those 30 days is granted on the second visit. Extension: the DI&E 'How to Extend Short Visit ETA' page says a short visit visa can be extended up to a maximum of 270 days from arrival (30 days on entry, 60 days at the first extension, 90 days at the second and third), applied for at the Visa Section of the Department of Immigration & Emigration head office (Battaramulla) or via the online e-Visa Extension portal (eservices.immigration.gov.lk) 'for extension up to 6 months'; the 'How to submit an ETA application' page instead says the ETA 'can be extended for up to six months' — the two DI&E pages conflict, so the safe reading is up to 6 months unless the department confirms more. Extension fees are charged even for holders of a free ETA. Other ETA rules from DI&E: an ETA holder must enter within three months of the ETA's issue (the FAQ separately says an ETA 'is valid for six months' — a conflict on the same site); you cannot obtain a fresh ETA while inside Sri Lanka; fees are non-refundable. A visa on arrival is also listed in the fee table (US$60 tourist for non-South-Asian nationals), but DI&E states all foreign nationals 'are required to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) prior to their arrival', so apply in advance. Beware lookalike paid ETA sites — the only official portal is eta.gov.lk. Children under 12 of any nationality get a free 30-day tourist ETA. Documents and extension rules are from the same eta.gov.lk site: visainfo/apply.jsp (port-of-entry requirements), visainfo/extsheta.jsp (extensions), visainfo/center.jsp and visainfo/faq.jsp.

A visa lets you stay up to 30 days from entry; longer stays need a Visitor's Permit Extension at an immigration office.

documentsNeeded: Ordinary passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry to Peru
Entry is recorded digitally at international airports (virtual Tarjeta Andina de Migración, TAM); if entering by land, make sure your passport is stamped
Immigration/customs may ask for a return or onward ticket, accommodation details and proof of sufficient funds
notes: Austria ordinary passport holders are visa-exempt for tourism and business in Peru (Foreign Ministry table, PDF dated 16 Jul 2026, legal basis listed as bilateral agreement N° B-3929; the table also cites D.S. N° 022-2016-RE ratifying the Peru–EU short-stay visa-waiver agreement). The term is '90***', defined as '90 days every 180 days from the first entry into national territory' — a 90-in-180-day rule like Schengen's, which we model as a 180-day rolling window. No extension is mentioned for this category. Passport validity: the Embassy of Peru in Singapore's visa FAQ (gob.pe, 22 Mar 2026) says the passport 'must have a minimum of 6 months validity from the date of entry to Peru'; the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice say the same. Air arrivals are not stamped; Migraciones records entry digitally (virtual TAM) and you can check your authorised stay online at Migraciones; land arrivals must get an entry stamp (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Global Affairs Canada says officials may ask for a return/onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, and that overstaying incurs a fine for each day, payable on exit. Law: Decreto Legislativo 1350 (Migraciones) as amended by D.Leg. 1582 (El Peruano) sets the tourist stay at 'up to 183 calendar days, cumulative over a 365-day period counted from the first regular entry', or the shorter term fixed in a visa-waiver agreement; where less than 183 days is granted an extension can be granted up to that limit unless the agreement sets a lower term or forbids extension. Tourist status does not allow paid work.

documentsNeeded: Valid machine-readable passport (valid at least 1 day on entry; your stay cannot exceed its expiry)
Return or onward ticket (or navigation plan naming the destination port)
Proof of funds: at least US$100 per month or part-month of stay
Customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) on arrival
notes: Costa Rica's current visa directive (AJ-484-11-2025, in force since publication 17 Nov 2025; it repealed the Oct 2023 directive DG-30-10-2023-AJ) lists ANDORRA in the FIRST GROUP: 'INGRESO SIN VISA. PERMANENCIA MÁXIMA: HASTA 180 DÍAS NATURALES NO PRORROGABLES. (Únicamente se prorrogará a quienes se le otorguen menos de 90 días y hasta por un máximo de 90 días). VIGENCIA MÍNIMA DE PASAPORTE: HASTA UN DÍA (el plazo de permanencia otorgado por el oficial de control migratorio, no será mayor al de la vigencia del pasaporte).' So: no visa; the border officer decides the stay, up to 180 calendar days counted from entry (per entry — the directive sets no cumulative cap across trips), and never beyond the passport's expiry; your passport only needs to be valid on the day of entry, but a longer validity buys a longer stay. The stay cannot be extended unless the officer granted fewer than 90 days, in which case an extension of up to 90 days can be requested (the text does not say whether 90 is the extra time or the total). Check the stamp: the days granted are what count, not the 180-day ceiling. Entry requirements for every foreigner (Directrices, PRIMERO §4, citing art. 42 Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 and art. 30 Reglamento de Control Migratorio 36769-G): a valid, machine-readable/biometric passport in good condition; a visa where required; proof of funds of at least US$100 per month or part-month of authorised stay; a return or onward ticket (or a navigation plan naming the destination port); and no bar to entry. Tourist (No Residente, subcategoría Turismo) status allows leisure, business or professional activities only if they involve no pay or profit in Costa Rica. Also on arrival: a customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) is required of every arriving traveller (art. 368 Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto 44051-H). Per the UK FCDO page (cross-check), a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow-fever transmission risk, an air departure tax of US$29 may apply (usually included in the ticket), and overstayers can be fined US$100 per month and refused future entry; travel.gc.ca (updated 31 Aug 2026) adds that people deported for overstaying may be barred from re-entering for 5 to 10 years.

Return or onward ticket (or navigation plan naming the destination port)
Proof of funds: at least US$100 per month or part-month of stay
Customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) on arrival
notes: Costa Rica's current visa directive (AJ-484-11-2025, in force since publication 17 Nov 2025; it repealed the Oct 2023 directive DG-30-10-2023-AJ) lists HUNGRÍA in the FIRST GROUP: 'INGRESO SIN VISA. PERMANENCIA MÁXIMA: HASTA 180 DÍAS NATURALES NO PRORROGABLES. (Únicamente se prorrogará a quienes se le otorguen menos de 90 días y hasta por un máximo de 90 días). VIGENCIA MÍNIMA DE PASAPORTE: HASTA UN DÍA (el plazo de permanencia otorgado por el oficial de control migratorio, no será mayor al de la vigencia del pasaporte).' So: no visa; the border officer decides the stay, up to 180 calendar days counted from entry (per entry — the directive sets no cumulative cap across trips), and never beyond the passport's expiry; your passport only needs to be valid on the day of entry, but a longer validity buys a longer stay. The stay cannot be extended unless the officer granted fewer than 90 days, in which case an extension of up to 90 days can be requested (the text does not say whether 90 is the extra time or the total). Check the stamp: the days granted are what count, not the 180-day ceiling. Entry requirements for every foreigner (Directrices, PRIMERO §4, citing art. 42 Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 and art. 30 Reglamento de Control Migratorio 36769-G): a valid, machine-readable/biometric passport in good condition; a visa where required; proof of funds of at least US$100 per month or part-month of authorised stay; a return or onward ticket (or a navigation plan naming the destination port); and no bar to entry. Tourist (No Residente, subcategoría Turismo) status allows leisure, business or professional activities only if they involve no pay or profit in Costa Rica. Also on arrival: a customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) is required of every arriving traveller (art. 368 Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto 44051-H). Per the UK FCDO page (cross-check), a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow-fever transmission risk, an air departure tax of US$29 may apply (usually included in the ticket), and overstayers can be fined US$100 per month and refused future entry; travel.gc.ca (updated 31 Aug 2026) adds that people deported for overstaying may be barred from re-entering for 5 to 10 years.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay until departure (special tourist measure valid to 31 Dec 2026; normally 6 months' validity required)
E-Ticket electronic entry/exit form, completed before travel (mandatory on entry and exit)
Tourist Card (US$10; included in the airfare for air arrivals) unless exempt by bilateral agreement
Proof of onward or return travel (may be requested)
notes: The Dominican Foreign Ministry (MIREX) visa-requirements tool, queried for Austria / ordinary passport / tourist visa (TS), answers '¿Requiere visa? NO'. UK and Canadian government advice both say tourists can visit visa-free for up to 30 days. Stay: the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) service page 'Prórroga de estadía para turistas' (migracion.gob.do/servicio/prorroga-de-estadia/) says tourists are allowed '30 días establecidos para los turistas' and that a stay of more than 30 days can be authorised 'a través de una prórroga extensible hasta 120 días'. Extension: apply online at the DGM portal (personal.migracion.gob.do / servicios.migracion.gob.do) with a copy of the passport data page, the stamp/date of last entry, a return air ticket, proof of own funds and a medical certificate; processing three working days; the application is free but the stay fee is charged: RD$3,500 for 30–90 days and RD$5,600 for 90–120 days, payable online or at the airport. Overstay: DGM's 'Servicio de cálculo y pago de tasas de estadía' says foreigners who exceed their authorised stay regularise it on departure by paying the stay fee (table: 30–90 days RD$3,500; 3–9 months RD$5,600; 9–12 months RD$7,000; rising to RD$98,000 for 10 years plus RD$7,000 per extra year), calculated at stayfee.migracion.gob.do. DGM's FAQ adds that if the stay fee is paid in advance at DGM you then have 30 days to leave. Canada's travel advice (travel.gc.ca, updated 26 May 2026) says to request the extension before the tourist card expires and that overstayers 'could be deported or refused re-entry'. Arrival form: DGM states the electronic E-Ticket (eticket.migracion.gob.do) is mandatory for every passenger on entry and on exit (combined migration and customs declaration, laws 285-04, 115-17, 72-02 and 226-06); UK advice says it can be completed up to 7 days before arrival and gives a QR code. Tourist card: the tax authority DGII says foreigners entering without a consular visa must have a Tourist Card (US$10, or €10 at sea/land ports only), with exemptions for nationals covered by bilateral agreements ratified by Congress; for air arrivals its cost is included in the airline ticket. The MIREX tool does not say whether this nationality is card-exempt. UK and Canadian advice both say you may be asked for proof of onward/return travel; Canada adds proof of adequate funds and your address in the country. Passport: under DGM's measure announced 2 December 2025 (memorandum continuing Resolución DGM-01-2024 of 31 May 2024), citizens of Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, the USA, 'Inglaterra' and EU countries travelling exclusively for tourism need a passport valid only for the length of their stay and departure, instead of the 6-month minimum 'que usualmente se exige'. This applies from 1 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2026 — re-check for travel in 2027.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport (valid for the whole stay)
notes: Argentina's immigration authority (Dirección Nacional de Migraciones, DNM) lists no visa requirement for ordinary passports of this nationality in its 'Régimen de Visas' table (read 2026-10-09). Argentina's official tourist-entry page (argentina.gob.ar/migraciones/documentacion-para-ingresar-al-pais-como-turista) says tourists may stay 'hasta TRES (3) MESES PRORROGABLE POR OTRO PERÍODO SIMILAR' (up to 3 months, extendable once for a similar period) and may not do paid work; the Cancillería tourist-visa page and consulates express the tourist stay as 90 days, so it is modelled as 90 days per entry. Extension: request it from Migraciones before your permitted stay ends; no fee was stated on the pages read. Health insurance: Decreto 366/2025 (Boletín Oficial 29/05/2025) changed art. 34 of Migration Law 25.871 so that foreigners must present a sworn declaration of the purpose of entry and that they hold health insurance, but its new art. 123 bis says that declaration 'será exigible una vez reglamentada su implementación' (only enforceable once regulated); no implementing regulation was found as of 2026-10-09, so it is not listed as a required document. Outside emergencies, national public hospitals may charge foreigners without permanent residence (new art. 8), so insurance is strongly advisable. Cross-check not possible: travel.state.gov was blocked (Cloudflare) from this environment; status rests on the DNM table.

Extension: request it from Migraciones before your permitted stay ends; no fee was stated on the pages read. Outside emergencies, national public hospitals may charge foreigners without permanent residence (new art. 8), so insurance is strongly advisable. Health insurance: Decreto 366/2025 (Boletín Oficial 29/05/2025) changed art. 34 of Migration Law 25.871 so that foreigners must present a sworn declaration of the purpose of entry and that they hold health insurance, but its new art. 123 bis says that declaration 'será exigible una vez reglamentada su implementación' (only enforceable once regulated); no implementing regulation was found as of 2026-10-09, so it is not listed as a required document. Outside emergencies, national public hospitals may charge foreigners without permanent residence (new art. 8), so insurance is strongly advisable. Cross-check not possible: travel.state.gov was blocked (Cloudflare) from this environment; status rests on the DNM table.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay
Onward or return ticket (may be requested at the border)
Proof of sufficient funds (may be requested at the border)
notes: Visa-free under the EU–Colombia short-stay visa waiver agreement (in force since December 2015): Art. 4(1) 'Citizens of the Union may stay in the territory of Colombia for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period'; Art. 4(3) leaves Colombia free to extend beyond 90 days under national law. Modelled as the agreement's 90 days in any rolling 180-day window. Under Colombian national law a Tourism Permit is up to 90 days per entry and can be extended by a PTP 'prórroga' of up to 90 days, never beyond 180 days per calendar year; per Resolución 0599 de 2026 Art. 2 and Migración Colombia's PTP page, citizens of European Union countries are exempt from the COP 150,000 PTP fee ('UNIÓN EUROPEA - PTP - Prórroga COP 0'). Apply online at least 5 business days before the permit expires; grant is discretionary. Entry documents (Migración Colombia): valid passport, plus onward ticket and proof of funds 'según corresponda'. Check-Mig online pre-registration: Migración Colombia and the UK's advice say it's free and not mandatory, while some European governments' advice says it's required within 72 hours before entry and exit. Paid activities require a visa (the agreement excludes paid activity). Yellow-fever certificate needed if arriving from certain transmission-risk countries (gov.uk).

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months after your departure date from the Bahamas
Return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas
Proof of sufficient funds for the stay (or a local sponsor who will receive you)
Completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
Yellow fever vaccination certificate only if arriving from (or transiting >12 hours through) a country with yellow fever risk
notes: Visa-free for up to 3 months. Bahamas Immigration's 'Before Your Arrival' page (updated 4 Nov 2026) lists 'Austria' among countries whose diplomatic, official and ordinary passport holders 'do not need a visa to enter The Bahamas for a stay up to three (3) months.' The source states 3 months; 90 days used as the safe figure. The officer records the period granted in your passport, and it may be shorter. Entry criteria (Bahamas Immigration 'Before Your Arrival', updated 4 Nov 2026, under the Immigration Act, Chapter 191, Section 22): a valid return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas, no gainful employment, financial means for the stay (or a local sponsor), a passport valid for at least six months (passport cards not accepted) and a completed Disembarkation/Embarkation Card; 'admittance is not automatic', and leave to land may be refused even when these are met. How long you may stay is decided at the border: the period granted 'is recorded in your passport and is at the discretion of the Immigration Officer at the port of entry', up to 'a maximum of eight (8) months, depending on nationality' (Immigration 'Entry Requirements', updated 5 Nov 2026). Extensions: apply to the Department of Immigration before the period granted expires; in-person interview with an extension officer; non-refundable processing fee of $200.00; bring your passport, return ticket, the Immigration Landing Card, the reason for the extension, a local address, an email address and mobile number, and your sponsor's passport and address if applicable (Immigration 'Extension of Stay', updated 5 Nov 2026). Overstaying is a punishable offence. Yellow fever certificate required from travellers over 1 year arriving from (or transiting more than 12 hours through) a listed risk country (including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Kenya and others), vaccinated at least 10 days before entry.

documentsNeeded: Bahamian visa obtained before travel
Passport valid for at least 6 months
Return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas
Proof of sufficient funds (or local sponsor)
Completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
notes: Visa required. Bahamas Immigration's 'Before Your Arrival' page (updated 4 Nov 2026) lists 'Albania' among countries whose diplomatic, official and ordinary passport holders 'must obtain a visa to enter The Bahamas'. Visas are issued before travel by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (online eVISA or a listed consulate); citizens of countries requiring Bahamian visas who try to enter without one 'would be refused leave to land.' Entry criteria (Bahamas Immigration 'Before Your Arrival', updated 4 Nov 2026, under the Immigration Act, Chapter 191, Section 22): a valid return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas, no gainful employment, financial means for the stay (or a local sponsor), a passport valid for at least six months (passport cards not accepted) and a completed Disembarkation/Embarkation Card; 'admittance is not automatic', and leave to land may be refused even when these are met. How long you may stay is decided at the border: the period granted 'is recorded in your passport and is at the discretion of the Immigration Officer at the port of entry', up to 'a maximum of eight (8) months, depending on nationality' (Immigration 'Entry Requirements', updated 5 Nov 2026). Extensions: apply to the Department of Immigration before the period granted expires; in-person interview with an extension officer; non-refundable processing fee of $200.00; bring your passport, return ticket, the Immigration Landing Card, the reason for the extension, a local address, an email address and mobile number, and your sponsor's passport and address if applicable (Immigration 'Extension of Stay', updated 5 Nov 2026). Overstaying is a punishable offence. Yellow fever certificate required from travellers over 1 year arriving from (or transiting more than 12 hours through) a listed risk country (including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Kenya and others), vaccinated at least 10 days before entry.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole intended stay (the permit cannot run past the travel document's expiry)
Proof of sufficient means of support for the stay, if asked

Joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration (Declaración Jurada) on arrival — the form says it must be filled out by every person entering Chile; adults (18+) include accompanying minors' baggage; digital version available for Santiago airport and land border crossings, or on paper
notes: Chile's Foreign Ministry visa table (Cuadro de aranceles de visas de permanencia transitoria, PDF created 6 March 2026, linked from consulado.gob.cl and from SERMIG's tourist page) lists AUSTRIA as 'NO' under '¿Requiere visa de permanencia transitoria?' with a maximum stay ('plazo máximo estadía') of 90 days, fee US$0. So ordinary-passport holders visit visa-free for up to 90 days per entry. General rules (Servicio Nacional de Migraciones, 'Permanencia Transitoria', updated 14 Oct 2025): visitors enter as holders of a Permanencia Transitoria permit, which allows a stay 'por hasta 90 días' and cannot run past the validity of the travel document; the PDI (Policía de Investigaciones) records the permitted period on the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) at entry; visitors must have 'los medios económicos suficientes para sustentar su estadía' and may not do paid work. Extension (SERMIG 'Prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria', updated 30 Jun 2026): 'hasta noventa días corridos', 'por una sola vez', applied for online in SERMIG's Portal de Trámites Digitales before the period on your TUM expires; fee USD 100 (children and adolescents exempt); you must show means of support for the extension period and explain the reasons. Arrival: the joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration form states 'ESTA DECLARACIÓN DEBE SER LLENADA POR TODA PERSONA QUE INGRESE AL PAÍS' (adults 18+ sign and include minors' baggage); see the customs rows. The table's 'plazo máximo estadía' is the stay allowed on the permit; the 30/60/90-day figures are stated as days, not months.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least three months from the date of arrival in Israel
Approved ETA-IL electronic travel authorisation obtained before departure (fee 25 NIS, non-refundable)
notes: Israel's Population and Immigration Authority (PIBA) treats Austria as visa-exempt: its ETA-IL country data flags this nationality NEED_PERMIT=0 (checked 2026-11-02). PIBA: 'As of January 1st, 2025, travelers to Israel must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey.' An approved ETA-IL lets you travel to Israel and 'stay for up to 90 days per visit'; it is valid for up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first, and a new one (another 25 NIS) is needed with a new passport or a change of name, gender or citizenship. Every traveller including minors needs their own ETA-IL (an adult applies for a minor). Replies usually come within 24–72 hours; PIBA recommends applying at least 72 hours before booking flights or hotels. Apply only on the official site israel-entry.piba.gov.il. An ETA-IL 'does not constitute a guarantee of entry' — a border control officer decides at arrival, and it can be revoked for immigration or security reasons. Not exempt: people with Israeli citizenship (including dual nationals travelling on a foreign passport — they must show proof of Israeli citizenship to the airline) or holders of a valid Israeli visa. Stays beyond 90 days need an extension request under PIBA procedures (no fee or maximum stated on the pages read). Work is not allowed on an ETA-IL.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for your stay
Visa fee payable on arrival or online in advance (not exceeding USD 50 for a single-entry visa, USD 70 for multiple entry)
notes: Rwanda's DGIE grants visa on arrival to citizens of all countries (since 1 Jan 2018), for a 30-day visit. Fees 'must not exceed 50 USD for single entry visa or 70 USD for multiple entry', and are waived for citizens of African Union, Commonwealth and La Francophonie member countries; Austria isn't on Rwanda's named 90-day free-visa list. We haven't confirmed whether Austria counts as a Francophonie member for the fee waiver, so the fee line below may not apply to you. The visa can also be applied for online in advance via the Irembo government portal. Ebola: Rwanda screens arrivals at Kigali airport and restricts its border with the DRC; Germany's advice says foreign travellers who were in the DRC in the 30 days before arrival, even in transit, are refused entry.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for your stay
Visa fee payable on arrival or online in advance (not exceeding USD 50 for a single-entry visa, USD 70 for multiple entry)
notes: Rwanda's DGIE grants visa on arrival to citizens of all countries (since 1 Jan 2018), for a 30-day visit. Fees 'must not exceed 50 USD for single entry visa or 70 USD for multiple entry', and are waived for citizens of African Union, Commonwealth and La Francophonie member countries; Estonia isn't on Rwanda's named 90-day free-visa list. We haven't confirmed whether Estonia counts as a Francophonie member for the fee waiver, so the fee line below may not apply to you. The visa can also be applied for online in advance via the Irembo government portal. Ebola: Rwanda screens arrivals at Kigali airport and restricts its border with the DRC; Germany's advice says foreign travellers who were in the DRC in the 30 days before arrival, even in transit, are refused entry.

documentsNeeded: Approved Nigeria e-Visa (Tourism Visa – F5A) obtained online before travel, or an embassy-issued visa
Passport valid for at least 6 months
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
Online landing and departure cards, completed before entry and exit (Nigeria Immigration Service)
Online health declaration (Nigeria Health Declaration Form), completed before you travel
notes: The Nigeria Immigration Service states the Tourism Visa (F5A) is for "citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements". Austria is not an ECOWAS member, and no primary source found names it as having a visa-waiver agreement with Nigeria for ordinary passports (NIS publishes no such list). F5A terms (checked 2026-10-19): validity 90 days from issuance, single entry, stay of 30 days, not extendable, no employment. Fees were not verified — confirm on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng). Health declaration: Canada's travel advice says all travellers must complete an online health declaration form before travelling to Nigeria; the UK's says it's required for travellers coming from countries with Ebola transmission.

documentsNeeded: Approved Nigeria e-Visa (Tourism Visa – F5A) obtained online before travel, or an embassy-issued visa
Passport valid for at least 6 months
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
Online landing and departure cards, completed before entry and exit (Nigeria Immigration Service)
Online health declaration (Nigeria Health Declaration Form), completed before you travel
notes: The Nigeria Immigration Service states the Tourism Visa (F5A) is for "citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements". Croatia is not an ECOWAS member, and no primary source found names it as having a visa-waiver agreement with Nigeria for ordinary passports (NIS publishes no such list). F5A terms (checked 2026-10-19): validity 90 days from issuance, single entry, stay of 30 days, not extendable, no employment. Fees were not verified — confirm on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng). Health declaration: Canada's travel advice says all travellers must complete an online health declaration form before travelling to Nigeria; the UK's says it's required for travellers coming from countries with Ebola transmission.

notes: Visa-free: 'Albania' is on the list in Art. 3 literal A of Resolución 5488 de 2022 (as replaced by Resolución 12189 de 2026, in force since 4 September 2026), whose holders may 'ingresar, permanecer y salir de Colombia, exentos de requisito de visa' for airport transit or short-stay activities (short stay defined as under 90 days, extendable up to 180 days) that are not paid in Colombia. Colombian law: visitors from visa-exempt countries get a Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia (PIP) at the border. A Tourism Permit (PT) is 'hasta por noventa (90) días calendario' per entry (Resolución 3167 de 2019 Art. 14, Migración Colombia). notes: Visa-free: 'San Marino' is on the list in Art. 3 literal A of Resolución 5488 de 2022 (as replaced by Resolución 12189 de 2026, in force since 4 September 2026), whose holders may 'ingresar, permanecer y salir de Colombia, exentos de requisito de visa' for airport transit or short-stay activities (short stay defined as under 90 days, extendable up to 180 days) that are not paid in Colombia. Colombian law: visitors from visa-exempt countries get a Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia (PIP) at the border. A Tourism Permit (PT) is 'hasta por noventa (90) días calendario' per entry (Resolución 3167 de 2019 Art. 14, Migración Colombia). Migración Colombia counts each foreigner's days so they do not exceed 180 calendar days, continuous or discontinuous, in the same calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec). Extension: the Permiso Temporal de Permanencia (PTP, 'prórroga') extends a Tourism Permit by up to 90 more calendar days, never beyond 180 days in the calendar year; apply online (Formulario Único de Trámites) at least 5 business days before the PIP expires; 2026 fee COP 150,000 (Resolución 0599 de 2026); issued by email 3 business days after payment; grant is discretionary. Modelled here as 180 days in any 365-day window, which is stricter than the legal calendar-year count (the legal rule would allow, e.g., 180 days ending 31 Dec and a new allowance from 1 Jan) — and each single entry is still capped at 90 days unless extended. Entry documents (Migración Colombia 'Requisitos de entrada y salida del país'): valid passport, plus 'tiquete de viaje de salida y demostrar solvencia económica, según corresponda'; officers may also ask for invitation letters or lodging (Res. 3167/2019 Art. 8 par. 2). Any paid activity requires a visa. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 h to 1 h before travel) is free and explicitly 'no es de carácter obligatorio' per Migración Colombia; France's and Germany's advice say it's required before entry and exit and that airlines check it.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport — the Embassy of Jamaica in Washington says it should have at least six months' validity (UK, Canadian, French and Spanish government advice say valid for the duration of the stay; the six-month figure is the stricter one)
Return or round-trip ticket to a country you are admissible to
Evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself during the stay
Completed Immigration/Customs C5 form (online at enterjamaica.gov.jm, run by PICA and Jamaica Customs, or on paper on arrival)
Proof of vaccination against measles, rubella and polio
notes: Visa-free for tourist stays of up to 30 days, on one condition. The PICA Visa Unit country listing (13 March 2025) shows 'ESTONIA (poe)': 'NONE – 30 days or less as tourists (Effective May 10, 2016) providing they possess proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio' under 'Entry visa — foreigners arriving in Jamaica'. The listing marks the country '(poe)', and its key defines 'POE – visa issued at Port of Entry': without the vaccination proof, you get a Jamaican visa on arrival. Max visitor stay with extensions for non-Commonwealth citizens: 6 months (PICA). Common to all visitors (Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, 'Requirements for entry into Jamaica', embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/visitor_to_jamaica): national passport with 'at least six months' validity', a return or round-trip ticket, and 'evidence of sufficient funds'; 'the decision in respect of admission and length of stay in the country rests with the Immigration Officer' at the port of entry, so the date stamped in your passport is what counts. Every passenger completes the Immigration/Customs C5 card (PICA, 'Travel Documents Required': complete and sign the C5 online or on paper; the official online form is enterjamaica.gov.jm). Extension (PICA, 'Extension of Stay', pica.gov.jm/immigration/extension-of-stays): apply to PICA before your landing time expires; 'Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island' and 'Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor'; processed within three working days. PICA fee schedule (pica.gov.jm/immigration/fees, no effective date shown): extension of stay processing fee JM$10,000, and JM$50,000 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa-exemption period. Source dates: the March 2025 PICA PDF is the newest official country list found; PICA's own web table (pica.gov.jm/immigration/entry-visa-requirements) still says 'Last updated July 19, 2023'.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay in Mexico (no minimum validity beyond that)
FMM (Forma Migratoria Múltiple) tourist permit — generated electronically/on arrival for air travelers, or completed at land border crossings
notes: Austria is on Mexico's list of countries whose citizens don't need a visa to visit as tourists, in transit, or for business, technical activities, journalism or study, for up to 180 days without any pay in Mexico (Mexican Foreign Ministry, Consulate in Leamington). Mexican authorities don't require a minimum passport validity, but the passport must be valid for the whole stay. At an international airport the FMM is generated on entry; by land you fill it in. INM's FMM page says the form is valid for up to 180 calendar days from the entry stamp and covers one entry. Officers may ask for a hotel booking, return or onward tickets, and means of support. Visiting Quintana Roo (Cancún, Tulum, Playa del Carmen): the state charges foreign tourists an entry tax, payable online before or during the stay.

documentsNeeded: Either a Jamaican visa issued at the port of entry, or no Jamaican visa for up to 30 days as a tourist if you hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa and proof of vaccination against measles, rubella and polio

Valid passport — the Embassy of Jamaica in Washington says it should have at least six months' validity (UK, Canadian, French and Spanish government advice say valid for the duration of the stay; the six-month figure is the stricter one)
Return or round-trip ticket to a country you are admissible to
Evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself during the stay
Completed Immigration/Customs C5 form (online at enterjamaica.gov.jm, run by PICA and Jamaica Customs, or on paper on arrival)
notes: A visa is issued at the port of entry, unless you meet two conditions for visa-free tourist stays of up to 30 days. The PICA Visa Unit country listing (13 March 2025) shows 'BULGARIA (poe)': 'NONE – 30 days or less as tourists (Effective September 22, 2014) providing they have a USA, Canada, UK or Schengen Visa & possess proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio' under 'Entry visa — foreigners arriving in Jamaica'. The listing marks the country '(poe)', and its key defines 'POE – visa issued at Port of Entry': without the other visa and the vaccination proof, you get a Jamaican visa on arrival. The listing doesn't give that visa's fee or stay, so no day count is shown. Max visitor stay with extensions for non-Commonwealth citizens: 6 months (PICA). Common to all visitors (Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, 'Requirements for entry into Jamaica', embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/visitor_to_jamaica): national passport with 'at least six months' validity', a return or round-trip ticket, and 'evidence of sufficient funds'; 'the decision in respect of admission and length of stay in the country rests with the Immigration Officer' at the port of entry, so the date stamped in your passport is what counts. Every passenger completes the Immigration/Customs C5 card (PICA, 'Travel Documents Required': complete and sign the C5 online or on paper; the official online form is enterjamaica.gov.jm). Extension (PICA, 'Extension of Stay', pica.gov.jm/immigration/extension-of-stays): apply to PICA before your landing time expires; 'Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island' and 'Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor'; processed within three working days. PICA fee schedule (pica.gov.jm/immigration/fees, no effective date shown): extension of stay processing fee JM$10,000, and JM$50,000 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa-exemption period. Source dates: the March 2025 PICA PDF is the newest official country list found; PICA's own web table (pica.gov.jm/immigration/entry-visa-requirements) still says 'Last updated July 19, 2023'.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months on arrival (MOI). Note: GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France Diplomatie, Canada and NZ advise at least 6 months — carry 6 months to be safe with airlines
Confirmed return or onward ticket
Confirmed hotel reservation in Qatar for the visit, or a clear address of a friend/relative where you will stay

Health insurance from an insurance company accredited by Qatar's Ministry of Public Health (MOI lists it as a condition of the on-arrival visa; GOV.UK/Auswärtiges Amt describe it as mandatory for stays over 30 days)
notes: Qatar MOI page 'Free On-arrival Tourist Visa for 90 Days Non-extendable for (43) Countries' lists Austria. Conditions: '1- Passport valid for at least three months 2- Availability of confirmed return ticket 3- Hotel reservation at any hotel in Qatar during the visit period, or a clear address of a friend or relative. 4- Health insurance from an accredited insurance company.' The stay is free of charge and NOT extendable. Germany's Foreign Office describes this same waiver as valid for 180 days from issue, multiple entry, allowing at most 90 days of stay within that validity, so it is modelled as a rolling 90-days-in-180 window. Conflict noted: MOI requires passport validity of 3 months, but several travellers' governments (GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France, Canada, NZ) say 6 months; MOI is the controlling authority, documentsNeeded flags both. Health insurance: MOI lists 'Health insurance from an accredited insurance company' as a condition of every on-arrival category and its Entry Permits page says 'A valid health insurance policy from insurance companies registered with the Ministry of Public Health is required to enter Qatar', while GOV.UK and Auswärtiges Amt say it is compulsory for stays over 30 days (GOV.UK: standard premium QAR 50 per person per month). VisitQatar notes 'Visa-free entry is now the new term defining previously visa on arrival. Nothing changed except the name.' Entry is at the discretion of the border officer.

_sources.name: Ministry of Interior of the State of Qatar — Free On-arrival Tourist Visa for 90 Days Non-extendable for (43) Countries (list and conditions)

_sources.claim: Health insurance from a Ministry of Public Health-registered insurer required to enter; on-arrival visa overview
_sources.name: Ministry of Interior of the State of Qatar — Entry Permits (Visit Visas)

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months on arrival (MOI). Note: GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France Diplomatie, Canada and NZ advise at least 6 months — carry 6 months to be safe with airlines
Confirmed return or onward ticket
Confirmed hotel reservation in Qatar for the visit, or a clear address of a friend/relative where you will stay

Health insurance from an insurance company accredited by Qatar's Ministry of Public Health (MOI lists it as a condition of the on-arrival visa; GOV.UK/Auswärtiges Amt describe it as mandatory for stays over 30 days)
notes: Qatar MOI page 'Free On-arrival Tourist Visa for 90 Days Non-extendable for (43) Countries' lists Czech Republic. Conditions: '1- Passport valid for at least three months 2- Availability of confirmed return ticket 3- Hotel reservation at any hotel in Qatar during the visit period, or a clear address of a friend or relative. 4- Health insurance from an accredited insurance company.' The stay is free of charge and NOT extendable. Germany's Foreign Office describes this same waiver as valid for 180 days from issue, multiple entry, allowing at most 90 days of stay within that validity, so it is modelled as a rolling 90-days-in-180 window. Conflict noted: MOI requires passport validity of 3 months, but several travellers' governments (GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France, Canada, NZ) say 6 months; MOI is the controlling authority, documentsNeeded flags both. Health insurance: MOI lists 'Health insurance from an accredited insurance company' as a condition of every on-arrival category and its Entry Permits page says 'A valid health insurance policy from insurance companies registered with the Ministry of Public Health is required to enter Qatar', while GOV.UK and Auswärtiges Amt say it is compulsory for stays over 30 days (GOV.UK: standard premium QAR 50 per person per month). VisitQatar notes 'Visa-free entry is now the new term defining previously visa on arrival. Nothing changed except the name.' Entry is at the discretion of the border officer.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
Boarding card

Useful at the border if asked: travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, health/travel insurance covering your stay, accommodation details, and any invitation or letter explaining the purpose of your visit
notes: Andorra is on Ireland's non-visa-required list (official Immigration Service Delivery table), so no visa or pre-clearance is needed to visit. Ireland has no ETA-style pre-travel authorisation. On arrival by air or sea from outside the State you must present to an Immigration Officer, who decides how long you may stay — INIS: "up to a maximum of 3 months" — and stamps your passport; the officer can still refuse entry if not satisfied by your documents or explanations. Staying beyond 90 days requires applying to Immigration Service Delivery for permission. Ireland is not in Schengen: days here do not count toward the 90/180-day Schengen limit, and a Schengen visa or stay does not entitle you to enter Ireland. If you arrive via Northern Ireland you must still report to an Immigration Officer within 30 days (7 days if for business or employment).

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
notes: Bolivia's Foreign Ministry lists 'ARGENTINA' in Group I of its visa list: no tourist visa needed (Decreto Supremo 1923, art. 8, as amended in 2022). Bolivia's 2003 visa list (Decreto Supremo 27150, Annex I) already put it among countries needing no visa. Bolivia's migration regulation (Decreto Supremo 1923, art. 9) limits a tourist's stay to 90 calendar days a year at most. It doesn't say how the year is counted. Germany's travel advice reads it as the calendar year, with a new 90 days only after you leave Bolivia; we count any 365 days in a row, which never allows more than either reading. For British citizens, the UK government's travel advice says border officers issue 30-day stamps; check the days written on your entry stamp.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
notes: Bolivia's Foreign Ministry lists 'CROACIA' in Group I of its visa list: no tourist visa needed (Decreto Supremo 1923, art. 8, as amended in 2022). Germany's travel advice reads it as the calendar year, with a new 90 days only after you leave Bolivia; we count any 365 days in a row, which never allows more than either reading. documentsNeeded: Valid passport
Bolivian tourist visa, or an entry authorisation from the migration office
notes: Bolivia's Foreign Ministry lists 'ALBANIA' in Group II of its visa list. Bolivia's 2003 visa list (Decreto Supremo 27150, Annex II) put it among countries needing a visa without prior consultation. You need a tourist visa from a Bolivian consulate before you travel, or an entry authorisation from Bolivia's migration office, which has the same effect. The migration office issues it at land borders and airports when you couldn't reach a Bolivian consulate (Decreto Supremo 1923, arts. 8 and 10, as amended by Decreto Supremo 4828 of 2022). The visa or authorisation gives 30 days; the migration office can extend a tourist stay by up to 60 more days, and tourists may stay at most 90 calendar days a year.
